### Motivation
- Improve code clarity and maintainability for the update server by documenting its purpose and public endpoints.
- Make handler behavior and error conditions explicit for future contributors and automated tools.

### Description
- Added a module-level docstring to `update_server/server.py` that explains the server purpose and available endpoints (`GET /version` and `GET /download/{filename}`).
- Added a docstring to `get_version()` describing return value and the `HTTPException` cases when the version file is missing or unreadable.
- Added a docstring to `download_file(filename)` describing the `filename` argument, the returned `FileResponse`, and possible `HTTPException` error scenarios.
- Minor formatting newline adjustment at end of file.

- Ran `python -m py_compile update_server/server.py`, which completed successfully.

author: copilot
body:
Currently the app is only reachable when a local PC is running `python main.py`. This adds everything needed to deploy to a cloud platform so the app is accessible 24/7 from any device (mobile, iPad, LTE, etc.) without a running PC.

## Backend changes

- **`main.py`**: Added CORS middleware configurable via `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` env var; server `HOST`/`PORT` now read from environment (defaults to `0.0.0.0:8000`) — makes the app work behind Render/Heroku's port injection
- **`app/storage.py`**: `DATA_DIR` now configurable via env var; falls back to `./data` for local use; supports Render persistent disk or `/tmp/data` on free tier
- **`requirements.txt`**: Added `python-dotenv`

## Deployment config (new files)

- **`render.yaml`**: One-click Render Web Service deployment with `DATA_DIR=/tmp/data`
- **`Procfile`**: Heroku/Railway compatibility — `uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`
- **`.env.example`**: Documents `HOST`, `PORT`, `DATA_DIR`, `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`

## README

Added:
- Local vs cloud comparison table (external access, data persistence, cost, difficulty)
- Step-by-step Render deployment guide
- Environment variable reference table
- Note on ephemeral `/tmp` storage on free tier vs persistent disk on paid tier

> ⚠️ Free-tier Render instances reset `/tmp` on restart (~15 min inactivity). Persistent data requires a paid Render disk mounted at a custom `DATA_DIR`.

author: makubacki
body:
## Description

Closes #1453 

Adds project-level AI customization files to support AI-assisted code review.

These files encode Patina's domain-specific conventions so that AI reviewers can flag violations locally, prior to human review.

The files are layered:

1. Always-on instructions (.github/copilot-instructions.md): Covers global conventions across the codebase.

2. File-based instructions (.github/instructions/): Currently, provides component-specific instructions in components.instructions.md(applyTo: components/**) to supplement the global instructions. These load only when editing matching files to minimize token cost.

3. Review prompt file (.github/prompts/review.prompt.md): A reusable /review slash command that defines a structured review checklist. This is to provide a convenient way to reliably perform the same set of review steps. Delegates convention details to the always-on instructions to avoid duplication.

4. Reviewer agent (.github/agents/reviewer.agent.md): A read-only review persona restricted to `search` and `read` tool sets (no edit or execute tools). Includes a handoff to the default agent for implementing fixes after review.

References:

- VS Code Customization Overview: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/concepts/customization
- Custom Instructions: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/custom-instructions

author: dackclup
body:
Ethanol was rendering as Type = Natural Extract because
_applyPubchemProps overwrites mat.record.names.synonyms with PubChem's
synonym list (which for ethanol includes "Absolute ethanol",
"Anhydrous alcohol", etc.) and then _computeClassification re-runs
classifyMaterialType on the polluted record. The old
\b(absolute|wax|balsam|...)\b regex was evaluated over name + synonyms
+ desc + odorType, so "Absolute ethanol" triggered the natural_extract
branch.

Fixes, all inside classifyMaterialType (index.html only):

1. Drop synonyms from the keyword surface. Curated fields
   (name / note / odor_type / odor_description / usage_levels) are
   enough to identify a natural extract — real natural extracts are
   either in MIXTURES or carry an unambiguous keyword in their
   canonical name.
2. Narrow the natural_extract keyword set: evaluate only on
   (name + note), and drop "balsam" and "wax" — those false-positived
   on single molecules whose descriptions say "peru balsam-like"
   (Benzyl Cinnamate) or "waxy" notes. Peru/Tolu Balsam and Beeswax
   Absolute are all in MIXTURES and hit the MIXTURES check first.
3. Drop "additive" from the preservative-alternation regex (the
   /^(additive|base\/additive)$/ note check still handles explicit
   additive notes) so generic descriptions can't misfire.
4. Add a final pre-fallback rule: if a material has NO real odor AND
   its curated note/desc/odorType mentions solvent/carrier/diluent/
   emollient, OR its canonical name is one of the well-known
   formulation solvents/carriers (ethanol, dipropylene glycol,
   propylene glycol, isopropyl myristate, triethyl citrate, MCT oil,
   squalane, isododecane, benzyl benzoate), classify Type = additive.
   This gives Ethanol / DPG / IPM / PG / Squalane / MCT / etc. a
   domain-correct Type home while keeping solvent and carrier
   exclusively on the Function axis.
5. Relabel MATERIAL_TYPE_LABELS.additive and the Type filter radio
   from "Preservative / Additive" to just "Additive" so the label
   covers both preservative-class and solvent/carrier-class additives.

The 3-axis taxonomy (Type / Function / Industry) is unchanged.
"Solvent / Carrier" is NOT reintroduced as a Type. Filter counts and
card labels still read from the same FILTER_CACHE source of truth.

Verified (simulated classifier over the full DB):
- Ethanol → additive
- Dipropylene Glycol → additive
- Linalool / Hedione / Iso E Super / Vanillin / Musk Ambrette → aroma_chemical
- Peru Balsam / Tolu Balsam / Beeswax Absolute / Jasmine Oil / Rose Oil → natural_extract
- L-Menthol → natural_isolate
- Benzyl Cinnamate (previously FP) → aroma_chemical
- Distribution: 264 aroma_chemical, 126 natural_extract, 12 additive, 1 natural_isolate

author: jonathanbbiles
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent entry-scan skips caused by internal fetch churn by reusing cached data that is still within the trading freshness window instead of repeatedly hitting network endpoints and provoking rate/cooldown failures.
- Preserve all strategy gates and freshness semantics while reducing app-driven `stale_quote_primary` / `marketdata_unavailable` outcomes due to refetch churn.
- Provide better prefetch coverage (quotes + orderbooks) and telemetry so operators can verify that skips are from real market conditions rather than avoidable internal behavior.

### Description
- Added trading-usable accessors to the cache: `getQuoteUsable` and `getOrderbookUsable` in `backend/modules/marketDataCache.js`, which compute age from stored timestamps and expose `usable` when age <= caller `maxAgeMs` while leaving existing `getQuote`/`getOrderbook` intact.
- Updated `getOrFetchSymbolMarketData` (in `backend/modules/entryMarketDataContext.js`) to check the trading-usable cache first (using the requested `quoteMaxAgeMs` / `orderbookMaxAgeMs`) and to fall back to usable cache when coordinator fetches return `rate_limited`, `cooldown_active`, or `stale_unusable/marketdata_unavailable`; new response states `cache_layer_usable` and `cache_fallback_after_failure` were added and stats `usableCacheReuses` and `cacheFallbacksAfterFailure` are tracked.
- Extended prefetch flow in `backend/trade.js` to batch-prefetch quotes (new `ENTRY_PREFETCH_QUOTES` flag) and to enable orderbook prefetch by default in live defaults, seeding the scan-local cache with `upsertQuote`/`upsertOrderbook` and exposing `prefetchedQuotes` / `prefetchedOrderbooks` telemetry in `marketDataBudget`.
- Added runtime/config wiring and docs: `ENTRY_PREFETCH_QUOTES` added to `backend/config/runtimeConfig.js`, defaulted to `true` in `backend/config/liveDefaults.js` and example envs/README updated; `ENTRY_PREFETCH_ORDERBOOKS` default set to `true` for live examples.

### Testing
- Ran unit/behavioral tests: `node modules/marketDataCache.test.js`, `node modules/entryMarketDataContext.test.js`, `node config/runtimeConfig.test.js`, `node config/liveDefaults.test.js`, and the repo-level `node trade.test.js`, and verified they passed after fixes (tests validate usable-cache semantics, usable-cache-before-fetch, fallback-on-rate-limit/cooldown/unavailable, prefetch seeding, and config defaults).
- Test highlights: cache accessor test verifies a 5s-old quote is `usable` under a 30s `maxAgeMs` while TTL `fresh` remains strict, entry-context tests verify usable-cache-first and fallback reuse on coordinator failures, and trade tests verify prefetch warmers seed the scan cache; all updated tests completed successfully in the validation run.
- Observability validated by inspecting `marketDataBudget` fields in end-of-scan summaries which now include `prefetchedQuotes`, `prefetchedOrderbooks`, `usableCacheReuses`, and `cacheFallbacksAfterFailure` indicating prefetch and cache-reuse activity.
- No strategy thresholds, gates, or freshness limits were loosened; tests for gating logic were not altered and continue to pass.

This PR updates [pytest](https://pypi.org/project/pytest) from **7.0.1** to **9.0.3**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 9.0.3
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `12444 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12444>`_: Fixed :func:`pytest.approx` which now correctly takes into account :class:`~collections.abc.Mapping` keys order to compare them.


- `13634 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13634>`_: Blocking a ``conftest.py`` file using the ``-p no:`` option is now explicitly disallowed.

  Previously this resulted in an internal assertion failure during plugin loading.

  Pytest now raises a clear ``UsageError`` explaining that conftest files are not plugins and cannot be disabled via ``-p``.


- `13734 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13734>`_: Fixed crash when a test raises an exceptiongroup with ``__tracebackhide__ = True``.


- `14195 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14195>`_: Fixed an issue where non-string messages passed to `unittest.TestCase.subTest()` were not printed.


- `14343 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14343>`_: Fixed use of insecure temporary directory (CVE-2025-71176).



Improved documentation
----------------------

- `13388 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13388>`_: Clarified documentation for ``-p`` vs ``PYTEST_PLUGINS`` plugin loading and fixed an incorrect ``-p`` example.


- `13731 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13731>`_: Clarified that capture fixtures (e.g. ``capsys`` and ``capfd``) take precedence over the ``-s`` / ``--capture=no`` command-line options in :ref:`Accessing captured output from a test function <accessing-captured-output>`.


- `14088 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14088>`_: Clarified that the default :hook:`pytest_collection` hook sets ``session.items`` before it calls :hook:`pytest_collection_finish`, not after.


- `14255 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14255>`_: TOML integer log levels must be quoted: Updating reference documentation.



Contributor-facing changes
--------------------------

- `12689 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12689>`_: The test reports are now published to Codecov from GitHub Actions.
  The test statistics is visible `on the web interface
  <https://app.codecov.io/gh/pytest-dev/pytest/tests>`__.

  -- by :user:`aleguy02`
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.0.2
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `13896 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13896>`_: The terminal progress feature added in pytest 9.0.0 has been disabled by default, except on Windows, due to compatibility issues with some terminal emulators.

  You may enable it again by passing ``-p terminalprogress``. We may enable it by default again once compatibility improves in the future.

  Additionally, when the environment variable ``TERM`` is ``dumb``, the escape codes are no longer emitted, even if the plugin is enabled.


- `13904 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13904>`_: Fixed the TOML type of the :confval:`tmp_path_retention_count` settings in the API reference from number to string.


- `13946 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13946>`_: The private ``config.inicfg`` attribute was changed in a breaking manner in pytest 9.0.0.
  Due to its usage in the ecosystem, it is now restored to working order using a compatibility shim.
  It will be deprecated in pytest 9.1 and removed in pytest 10.


- `13965 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13965>`_: Fixed quadratic-time behavior when handling ``unittest`` subtests in Python 3.10.



Improved documentation
----------------------

- `4492 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4492>`_: The API Reference now contains cross-reference-able documentation of :ref:`pytest's command-line flags <command-line-flags>`.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.0.1
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `13895 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13895>`_: Restore support for skipping tests via ``raise unittest.SkipTest``.


- `13896 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13896>`_: The terminal progress plugin added in pytest 9.0 is now automatically disabled when iTerm2 is detected, it generated desktop notifications instead of the desired functionality.


- `13904 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13904>`_: Fixed the TOML type of the verbosity settings in the API reference from number to string.


- `13910 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13910>`_: Fixed `UserWarning: Do not expect file_or_dir` on some earlier Python 3.12 and 3.13 point versions.



Packaging updates and notes for downstreams
-------------------------------------------

- `13933 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13933>`_: The tox configuration has been adjusted to make sure the desired
  version string can be passed into its :ref:`package_env` through
  the ``SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST`` environment
  variable as a part of the release process -- by :user:`webknjaz`.



Contributor-facing changes
--------------------------

- `13891 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13891>`_, `#13942 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13942>`_: The CI/CD part of the release automation is now capable of
  creating GitHub Releases without having a Git checkout on
  disk -- by :user:`bluetech` and :user:`webknjaz`.


- `13933 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13933>`_: The tox configuration has been adjusted to make sure the desired
  version string can be passed into its :ref:`package_env` through
  the ``SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST`` environment
  variable as a part of the release process -- by :user:`webknjaz`.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.0.0
   ```
   =========================

New features
------------


- `1367 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1367>`_: **Support for subtests** has been added.

  :ref:`subtests <subtests>` are an alternative to parametrization, useful in situations where the parametrization values are not all known at collection time.

  Example:

  .. code-block:: python

      def contains_docstring(p: Path) -> bool:
          """Return True if the given Python file contains a top-level docstring."""
          ...


      def test_py_files_contain_docstring(subtests: pytest.Subtests) -> None:
          for path in Path.cwd().glob("*.py"):
              with subtests.test(path=str(path)):
                  assert contains_docstring(path)


  Each assert failure or error is caught by the context manager and reported individually, giving a clear picture of all files that are missing a docstring.

  In addition, :meth:`unittest.TestCase.subTest` is now also supported.

  This feature was originally implemented as a separate plugin in `pytest-subtests <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-subtests>`__, but since then has been merged into the core.

  .. note::

      This feature is experimental and will likely evolve in future releases. By that we mean that we might change how subtests are reported on failure, but the functionality and how to use it are stable.


- `13743 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13743>`_: Added support for **native TOML configuration files**.

  While pytest, since version 6, supports configuration in ``pyproject.toml`` files under ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]``,
  it does so in an "INI compatibility mode", where all configuration values are treated as strings or list of strings.
  Now, pytest supports the native TOML data model.

  In ``pyproject.toml``, the native TOML configuration is under the ``[tool.pytest]`` table.

  .. code-block:: toml

       pyproject.toml
      [tool.pytest]
      minver

author: justin-tahara
body:
## Description

The `cleanup-idle-sandboxes` task fans out per-tenant every 8 minutes in the cloud (`timedelta(minutes=1)` × `CLOUD_BEAT_MULTIPLIER_DEFAULT=8`). With ~20k tenants on the managed_services cluster, this fan-out is currently the dominant source of background database load — every 8 minutes the writer (`database-1-instance-3`) sees a ~600 AAS spike from `celery_worker_light_sync` running per-tenant `SELECT … FROM tenant_X.sandbox` queries, with massive catalog cache thrashing on the side.

`SANDBOX_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` defaults to 1 hour, so scanning more frequently than every ~15 minutes serves no functional purpose — a sandbox cannot become "newly idle" unless it has already been idle for an hour. Bumping the base schedule from 1 minute to 15 minutes makes the effective cloud cadence ~2 hours (15 min × 8x cloud multiplier), which still meets the idle-detection SLA, and immediately reduces the spike frequency by 15x.

This is a one-line change intended as the first of several fixes to the sandbox cleanup workflow. Follow-up PRs will add a Redis marker set so the task only fans out to tenants that actually have running sandboxes.

## How Has This Been Tested?

Verified the new schedule loads correctly via `get_cloud_tasks_to_schedule(8.0)` locally. No behavioral test added — the change is a single constant.

body:
Summary:
Reuse the existing `p` subblock pointer when initializing `b->start_` in `allocate_from_fixed_pools` instead of recomputing `b + 0x14`. This keeps the source plausible while aligning the generated pointer flow more closely with the original allocator.

Units/functions improved:
- `main/MSL_C/PPCEABI/bare/H/alloc`
- `allocate_from_fixed_pools`: 94.80556% -> 95.111115%

Progress evidence:
- `allocate_from_fixed_pools` diff-bearing instructions: 54 -> 47
- Unit `.text` match: 98.005264% -> 98.063156%
- `.rodata`, `.bss`, and `.sbss` were unchanged
- `ninja` rebuild completed successfully after the change

Plausibility rationale:
The function already computes `p` as the first fixed subblock in the newly allocated block. Assigning `b->start_ = p` is the natural source-level expression of that relationship and avoids recomputing the same address with a fresh cast.

Technical details:
Objdiff showed the prior code still emitted an extra `addi` to rebuild `b + 0x14` near the end of block initialization. Reusing `p` removes that recomputation and improves the generated register/value flow without adding any hacks, externs, or manual section tricks.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a faster, more user-friendly import workflow for commesse/cantieri from Excel/CSV and allow quick cached nearby searches for fuel/meals to improve responsiveness. 
- Reduce accidental silent failures when editing/deleting cantieri and make list actions attachable without inline `onclick` attributes. 
- Improve robustness of shared sync by increasing timeouts and surface timeout-specific feedback.

### Description
- UI: added `Importa commesse/cantieri (Excel)` button and hidden file input, and toggle its visibility depending on the selected catalog category. 
- Import: implemented `parseCommesseRowsFromMatrix`, `importCommesseRows`, and `importCommesseFromFile` to parse CSV/Excel (via XLSX), merge into existing commesse/cantieri, and sync after import. 
- Nearby search caching: added `nearbySearchPositionCache`, `nearbyFuelResultsCache`, `nearbyMealResultsCache` and helper functions `normalizeCoordsFromPosition`, `getNearbyResultCacheKey`, `readNearbyCache`, `writeNearbyCache`, and `getNearbySearchPositionFast` to reuse recent GPS and results. 
- Integrated caches into `findNearbyMealPlaces` and `findNearbyFuelStations` to render cached results immediately and refresh them, and call `ensureLeafletLoaded` without awaiting to avoid blocking UI. 
- Replaced inline `onclick` on cantieri list with `data-action` attributes and attached event listeners that call `editCantiereFromDataHub`/`deleteCantiereFromDataHub`. 
- Improved error handling in `deleteCantiereFromDataHub` to show messages when commessa/cantiere not found. 
- Sync/timing: increased default shared sync timeouts in `runSharedSyncCycle` and `autoSyncOnDeviceAccess`, added `isTimeoutSyncError` helper, and show a non-fatal message when auto-sync times out. 

### Testing
- Ran static checks and a build step (`eslint` and project build) which completed successfully. 
- Performed automated parsing validation on sample CSV/Excel matrices via the added `parseCommesseRowsFromMatrix` logic in unit-like smoke runs which succeeded. 
- Verified that cached nearby-search flows return cached entries and that fresh fetches update the cache in automated integration-like runs which succeeded.

author: yezhizhen
body:
During traversal, exclude shadow roots.

Analysis:
Each shadow root is processed twice:
- via host: Element::bind_to_tree()
-  Via iterator

In total, this would be
```math
\sum_{i=0}^{N-1} 2^i = 2^N - 1
```

Testing: Added a test.
Fixes: https://github.com/servo/servo/issues/43998

body:
## Summary

- Add `parse_where_clause()` to `parse_struct_def`, `parse_enum_def`, and `parse_trait_def` — the parser previously accepted where clauses only on functions and impl blocks, not on type definitions
- Fix `parse_where_clause` to handle `Self` (keyword) as the LHS of a predicate; previously `where Self: Sized` caused a parse error
- Add fixture `tests/fixtures/fls_4_14_where_clauses_on_types.rs` with examples of all three forms
- Add 16 milestone 141 tests (compile-and-run + assembly inspection) verifying struct/enum/trait with where clauses compile to correct ARM64

**FLS §4.14 AMBIGUOUS**: The spec does not specify when where-clause bounds on type definitions are checked (parse time, type-check, or monomorphization time). Galvanic parses and discards the bounds; the concrete type is inferred from call-site arguments.

author: 8dionysus
body:
## What changed

- land the first diagnostic spine source-of-truth in `docs/DIAGNOSTIC_SPINE.md`
- add runtime-owned diagnostic contracts and examples for:
  - `diagnostic_target_v1`
  - `diagnostic_session_v1`
  - `diagnosis_companion_v1`
  - `diagnostic_anchor_ref_v1`
  - `repair_handoff_v1`
  - `reviewed_diagnosis_ref_v1`
- add the read-only `scripts/aoa-diagnose` seam and `scripts/_aoa_diagnose.py`
- wire quest follow-through with `ABYSS-STACK-Q-0007`
- extend layout checks, validator coverage, workflow coverage, and contract tests
- keep the repo-local skill surface thin and sourced from canonical `aoa-skills`

## Why

This lands the self-diagnosis groundwork as a runtime-owned read model with explicit handoff toward self-repair, without widening mutation authority.

The goal is to prepare the stack for honest diagnosis and repair routing while preserving these boundaries:

- `aoa-doctor` stays readiness-only
- skill canon stays in `aoa-skills`
- `aoa-diagnose` stays descriptive and citation-friendly
- repair remains explicit and review-gated

## Impact

- the stack can now materialize structured runtime diagnostic artifacts under `Logs/diagnostics/`
- repair posture is now bridgeable through explicit reviewed diagnosis refs instead of implicit promotion
- source/deployed parity for the new sync-managed surfaces is enforced by validation
- the live runtime was rechecked after sync and returned to a green `running_as_intended` posture, with `last_good.ref.json` refreshed

## Validation

- `python -m py_compile scripts/_aoa_diagnose.py scripts/validate_stack.py`

## Notes

author: honry
body:
### Details:

Some frameworks decompose GroupNormalization via InstanceNormalization and reshape the grouped tensor directly to 4D {N,G,-1,1} with a trailing unit dimension. MVN then reduces over axes {2,3} instead of axis {2} as in the existing 3D pattern {N,G,-1}. This is mathematically equivalent since the trailing dimension is always 1.

Changes:
- Extend `pre_mvn_reshape_m` predicate from `rank_equals(3)` to `is_rank_3_or_4` so the pattern matcher accepts both 3D and 4D reshapes before MVN.
- Validate the trailing dimension is 1 for the 4D variant.
- Handle MVN axes {2,3} validation for the 4D variant, including negative axis normalization.
- Allow concrete values (not just -1) in the pre-MVN reshape's third dimension, since some frameworks emit explicit flattened sizes after constant folding.
- Add positive tests for both special-marker ({0,G,-1,1}) and concrete-value 4D shapes, covering f32 and f16.
- Add negative edge-case tests: wrong MVN axes, single axis with 4D reshape, trailing dim != 1, axes over batch/groups, and three MVN axes.

### Tickets:
- CVS-184129

author: aaf2tbz
body:
## Summary

- Fix memory leak where `g_strdup()` allocates heap memory for `native_host_descriptor_.resourceDir` but it is never freed in the destructor or `close()` method
- Replace `g_strdup()` with a `std::string` member (`resource_dir_str_`) that manages its own lifetime automatically, and point `resourceDir` at its `c_str()`
- Remove `// FIXME leak` comment

## Details

The leak occurs at `src/plugins/carla_native_plugin.cpp:1247` — `g_strdup(res_dir)` allocates via GLib's allocator and stores the result in a raw `const char*` on the `NativeHostDescriptor` struct. The destructor calls `close()` which frees the host handle and plugin descriptor but never calls `g_free()` on this pointer.

The same file already uses the correct `g_free()` pattern at line 1007 for a similar allocation — this was simply an oversight.

The `std::string` approach is preferred because it eliminates the leak entirely through RAII, avoiding the need to add manual `g_free()` calls in `close()`.

## Files Changed

- `src/plugins/carla_native_plugin.h` — add `std::string resource_dir_str_;` member
- `src/plugins/carla_native_plugin.cpp` — replace `g_strdup()` with `resource_dir_str_` assignment

author: kovbo
body: Since Megatron runs in a subprocess, the serverless backend cannot reliably snapshot live training state by copying files from the parent process during long SFT runs. This PR changes internal checkpointing so the Megatron worker saves its own periodic checkpoints inside ART, and the serverless backend only uploads those intermediate checkpoints as artifacts for resume. This keeps the training logic in one place, makes long-running Megatron SFT jobs resumable after pod restarts or deploys, and leaves the final checkpoint to the normal end-of-training save path.

author: copilot
body:
The README sequence diagram had drifted from the actual implementation — wrong API endpoints, missing flows for two views, and a missing AI summary step in the batch flow.

## Corrections to existing flows

- **Flow 1 (HistoryView)** — fixed `alt` branch order to match code (`batch` → `single` → `url-analyzer`)
- **Flow 2 (URL Analyzer)** — corrected AI summary endpoint and payload:
  - `POST /api/summarize { reviews }` → `POST /api/deepseek/summary { text, overview, keywords }`
- **Flow 3 (Single Text Analysis)** — two fixes:
  - Save endpoint: `POST /api/history/save-report { userId, recordName, recordType, ... }` → `POST /api/history/save { userId, name, inputText, overview, keywords, sentences }`
  - Added missing `opt Generate AI Summary` block (`POST /api/deepseek/summary`)
- **Flow 4 (Batch CSV Analysis)** — added missing `opt Generate AI Summary` block + Growth Plan add-on flow after save

## New flows

- **Flow 5 — CompareView (`/compare`)**: fetches batch history + growth plans, supports reports vs plans comparison mode, generates AI comparative insight via `POST /api/deepseek/summary`
- **Flow 6 — GrowthPlanView (`/growth`)**: covers Create Plan, Delete Plan, Remove Data Point, and Replay Data Point (writes to `sessionStorage` and navigates to the appropriate analysis view for all three `sourceType` variants)

author: robdel12
body:
## Why
OrbitDock had two architecture-level problems that were surfacing as user-facing instability:

- We still had drift between legacy Codex policy strings (`approval_policy`, `sandbox_mode`) and canonical policy objects, which made policy behavior inconsistent across create/inspect/control-deck paths.
- Reconnect/session ownership timing had race windows (especially around direct-session hook routing and bootstrap-vs-delta ordering), which could require app restart to recover or show fresh data.

This PR moves us toward a single authoritative model for policy and a more reliable server/client state lifecycle for reconnect scenarios.

## What Changed
### 1) Canonical Codex policy handling (server-first)
- Threaded canonical approval/sandbox policy details through protocol/runtime/native surfaces.
- Kept legacy string fields as compatibility views, not primary truth.
- Updated selection/inspection behavior so canonical `*_details` are authoritative when mixed payloads contain both canonical and legacy fields.

### 2) Reconnect/session-state hardening
- Added immediate runtime ownership registration for direct Claude/Codex sessions before persistence flush, then reconciled with SQLite durability.
- Preserved cleanup behavior for stale/failed ownership claims.
- Fixed conversation refresh ordering so realtime row deltas are buffered during bootstrap and replayed after bootstrap completes.

### 3) Approval/control-deck fidelity
- Expanded Codex approval mapping and amendment flow support (`updated_input`) for network policy decisions.
- Improved native decode/presentation paths for canonical policy and approval data.

### 4) Supporting infra/tests/docs
- Added/updated runtime, persistence, lifecycle, and native tests for ownership, policy semantics, and reconnect behavior.
- Included planning docs/migration support tied to this rollout.

## Impact
- Reduces “must restart app to recover data” reconnect failure modes.
- Prevents mixed legacy/canonical payloads from applying stale policy values.
- Keeps compatibility with legacy clients while treating canonical policy as the source of truth.

## Validation
- `make test-unit` (pass)
- `cargo test -p orbitdock-server` (pass)
- `xcodebuild -project OrbitDockNative/OrbitDock.xcodeproj -scheme OrbitDock -destination 'platform=macOS' build` (pass)

## Scope
- This branch currently includes policy-alignment work plus reconnect/state-recovery fixes and related supporting changes vs `main`.

body:
Adds an optional `.github/workflows/aw.json` file for repository-level agentic workflow settings, starting with control over the `agentics-maintenance.yml` runner.

## Schema & Loading
- New JSON schema at `pkg/parser/schemas/repo_config_schema.json` (embedded, validated on load)
- Schema enforces a safe pattern on `runs_on` values, blocking control characters and newlines
- `pkg/workflow/repo_config.go` — loads, validates against schema, and deserialises into typed structs using JSON struct tags and `json.Unmarshal`
- `RunsOnValue` implements `json.Unmarshaler`, accepting either a JSON string or array of strings
- File is optional; absence returns safe defaults

## Supported Configuration

**Custom runner (string or array):**
```json
{
  "maintenance": {
    "runs_on": "my-custom-runner"
  }
}
```
```json
{
  "maintenance": {
    "runs_on": ["self-hosted", "linux"]
  }
}
```

**Disable maintenance entirely** (workflows using `expires` will emit a warning):
```json
{
  "maintenance": false
}
```

## Wiring
- All hardcoded `runs-on: ubuntu-slim` in `maintenance_workflow.go` replaced with the configured value (defaulting to `ubuntu-slim`)
- Multi-label `runs-on` values are serialised using `json.Marshal` to prevent YAML injection from special characters in runner labels
- `GenerateMaintenanceWorkflow` accepts a new `*RepoConfig` parameter; `nil` preserves existing behaviour
- Config loaded in `compile_post_processing.go` and `init.go` before maintenance workflow generation

body:
## Purpose
Establish comprehensive Playwright test infrastructure for MMGIS covering API, UI/map, tools, authentication, configuration, collaboration, performance, and accessibility. Consolidated from 14 parallel child sessions across 4 waves:

| Wave | Agents | Scope |
|------|--------|-------|
| 1 | A–D | Phase 0 infrastructure + API & security tests |
| 2 | E–H | Map UI, deep linking, draw/measure, tool panels |
| 3 | I–L | Time control, filtering, search, configure CMS, auth flows |
| 4 | M–N | WebSocket collaboration, performance, a11y, cross-browser, mobile |

**78 spec files** total across `tests/e2e/` and `tests/unit/`. No application source code was modified.

All child session PRs (#11–#20) have been closed — everything is consolidated here.

---

## Updates since last revision — port 18888, configure UI fixes, cross-browser Firefox filter, README accuracy

### Test port changed from 8888 to 18888

All test infrastructure now uses port **18888** instead of 8888 so developers can run tests while their dev server is running on 8888. Updated across **49 files**:
- `playwright.config.js` — `baseURL` default
- `tests/global-setup.js` — `TEST_PORT` constant
- `.github/workflows/playwright-tests.yml` — CI `PORT` env var
- `package.json` — `start:test` script (`PORT=18888`)
- All 47 test files with hardcoded `localhost:8888` references (including `tests/unit/stac-url-transformation.spec.js`)

### Configure UI test logic fixes

`layer-management.spec.js` and `tool-configuration.spec.js` checked for "Layers"/"Tools" text on the configure landing page **without first selecting a mission**. Tabs only appear after clicking a mission in the sidebar. Both tests now click `Reference-Mission` before asserting.

### Cross-browser Firefox JS error filter

Firefox reports null-access errors differently than Chromium (`"can't access property \"features\", a is null"` vs `"Cannot read properties of null"`). Added Firefox-specific patterns to the benign error filter in `basic-rendering.spec.js`:
- `!msg.includes("can't access property")`
- `!msg.includes('is null')`

### `start:test` script port mismatch (Devin Review)

The `start:test` npm script still had `PORT=8888` while all test infrastructure expected 18888. Fixed to `PORT=18888`.

### README: removed non-existent `global-teardown.js` (Devin Review)

The README directory tree listed `global-teardown.js` as a separate file, but teardown is handled by the function returned from `global-setup.js`. Updated to `global-setup.js — Global setup & teardown (...)`.

### Local validation (AUTH=off, all 12 suites, port 18888)

| Suite | Passed | Skipped | Failures |
|-------|--------|---------|----------|
| `test:e2e:api` | 90 | 46 | 0 |
| `test:e2e:auth-off` | 0 | 22 | 0 |
| `test:e2e:auth-local` | 15 | 7 | 0 |
| `test:e2e:security` | 30 | 5 | 0 |
| `test:e2e:startup` | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| `test:e2e:map` | 88 | 7 | 0 |
| `test:e2e:tools` | 19 | 19 | 0 |
| `test:e2e:configure` | 6 | 16 | 0 |
| `test:e2e:collaboration` | 6 | 7 | 0 |
| `test:e2e:performance` | 9 | 0 | 0 |
| `test:e2e:accessibility` | 8 | 1 | 0 |
| `test:e2e:mobile` | 5 | 0 | 0 |
| `test:e2e:cross-browser` | 10 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | **289** | **130** | **0** |

---

## Updates since last revision — auth fixes, cursor-sharing removal, cross-browser multi-project

### Auth test skip condition bug

The 5 auth spec files (`login-flow`, `signup-flow`, `session-management`, `authorization`, `password-management`) had a logical error in their skip conditions:

```js
// Before (broken — skips in BOTH AUTH=off AND AUTH=local):
test.skip(process.env.AUTH === 'off' || process.env.AUTH !== 'local', ...)

// After (correct — skips only when AUTH is not local):
test.skip(process.env.AUTH !== 'local', ...)
```

### Auth-local test fixes
- **`login-flow.spec.js`**: Changed `test_user` → `TEST_ADMIN` credentials. Only `test_admin` exists in a fresh DB (created by `globalSetup` via `first_signup`). `test_user` is never created.
- **`signup-flow.spec.js`**: Two UI tests (`signup toggle reveals signup fields`, `signup with new user credentials`) now check `#toggleWrapper` visibility at runtime and gracefully skip when `AUTH_LOCAL_ALLOW_SIGNUP=false` (the default). Previously they waited 10s for `#toggle` and timed out.

### Package.json typo fix
- `test:e2e:auth-off` had `AUTH=local` (copy-paste error) → fixed to `AUTH=off`

### Cursor-sharing tests removed
- Deleted `tests/e2e/collaboration/cursor-sharing.spec.js` (388 lines) — the cursor-sharing feature does not exist in MMGIS. The remaining collaboration tests (`multi-user.spec.js`, `websocket-connection.spec.js`) are retained.

### Cross-browser multi-project
- Firefox project enabled in `playwright.config.js` with `testMatch: /cross-browser/` so it **only** runs cross-browser specs. All other tests continue to run on chromium only.

---

## Updates since prior revision — race condition fix & server lifecycle overhaul

### Root cause: Playwright webServer starts BEFORE globalSetup

Playwright's internal task ordering runs `createPluginSetupTasks()` (which starts `webServer`) **before** `globalSetup`. This means the MMGIS server tried to connect to `mmgis-test` before `globalSetup` had a chance to create that database — causing `database "mmgis-test" does not exist` errors on fresh DBs.

### Fix: server lifecycle moved into globalSetup

Removed the `webServer` block from `playwright.config.js` entirely. The server is now started and stopped inside `tests/global-setup.js`, guaranteeing this order:

1. Create `mmgis-test` DB (if missing)
2. Set up PostGIS extensions + session table + schema migrations
3. Check if Reference Mission already exists
4. Start MMGIS server on port 18888
5. Wait for healthcheck (up to 120s)
6. Create admin user + Reference Mission via API (if needed)
7. Run all tests
8. Teardown function kills the server

### Other fixes in this round

- **Cross-platform compatibility**: Replaced all `curl` commands in global-setup with Node's native `fetch()` — works on Windows without requiring curl
- **Timeouts increased**: Global test timeout 2min → 3min, `waitForMapReady` default 60s → 90s, web server startup timeout 2min → 3min (helps on slower machines)
- **Devin Review bug fix**: `fetchJSON` returns raw HTML strings when JSON parsing fails (e.g. login page redirect). HTML strings are truthy, so the old `if (result)` check incorrectly reported Reference Mission creation as successful. Now checks `typeof result === 'object' && result.status === 'success'`.
- **Secrets baseline**: Removed stale `tests/global-setup.js` entry — `pragma: allowlist secret` inline comments now handle those lines

---

### Targeted `npm run test:e2e:{subtest}` scripts

Added 12 new npm scripts to `package.json` so developers can run specific test categories locally without running the full suite:

### CI scope reduced to lightweight tests only

The CI workflow's "Run E2E Tests" step was replaced with "Run E2E API Tests" that runs only:
```
npx playwright test tests/e2e/api tests/e2e/security tests/e2e/startup --project=chromium
```

author: giorey01
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: `decodeURIComponent` was called directly on untrusted user input (`params.slug`). If an invalid URL-encoded string is passed, it throws a `URIError`. In Next.js Server Components, this unhandled exception crashes the request rendering, resulting in a 500 Internal Server Error.
🎯 Impact: An attacker could intentionally request malformed URLs to cause repeated 500 errors, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) condition or resource exhaustion.
🔧 Fix: Wrapped the `decodeURIComponent(slug)` call in a `try...catch` block. If an error is caught, it logs a warning and falls back to using the raw un-decoded `slug` safely. 
✅ Verification: Ran `bun run lint`, `bun test`, and `bun run build`. All checks passed. Added a journal entry to `.jules/sentinel.md` to document the Next.js specific vulnerability regarding unhandled `decodeURIComponent` exceptions on untrusted dynamic route parameters.

### Motivation
- Introduce richer topic information into the memory write pipeline so topic inference can expose candidates, a selected topic, confidence and a classification status (classified/deferred). 
- Ensure low-confidence topic inferences do not produce noisy state updates by deferring state emission when classification confidence is below the threshold. 
- Preserve compatibility with existing storage (legacy `topic` field) while providing an authoritative `effectiveTopic` for runtime consumers. 

### Description
- Add new metadata types: `ClassificationStatus`, `TopicCandidate`, and `CoreMemoryMetadata` and helpers `CoreMemoryMetadata.fromTopicClassification` and `CoreMemoryMetadata.legacyTopic` in `lib/core/memory_runtime/entities/memory_runtime_models.dart`. 
- Extend `StatePatch`, `StateRecord`, and `MemoryUnit` to carry `CoreMemoryMetadata`, add `effectiveTopic` accessors, and implement `_decodeCoreMemoryMetadata` to backfill metadata from legacy `topic` values. 
- Implement defer rule and metadata population in the write pipeline by building `CoreMemoryMetadata` with a classification threshold (`0.5`) and skipping state emission when `classificationStatus == ClassificationStatus.deferred` or `confidence` is below policy in `lib/core/memory_runtime/services/rule_based_memory_runtime.dart`. 
- Update retrieval, scoring and context assembly to use metadata-driven `effectiveTopic` (selected topic or best candidate) instead of direct `topic` strings. 
- Add unit tests covering the confidence boundary behavior and legacy-to-metadata migration in `test/core/memory_runtime/services/topic_classification_metadata_test.dart`.

body:
# #50 Implemented Consumables Forecasting

This pull request introduces a comprehensive "Consumables Forecasting" feature for printer paper and ink, aimed at improving admin observability and proactive maintenance. It adds new API endpoints, database structures, and settings to track, store, and forecast consumable depletion, with a focus on supporting the Epson L5290 printer. The changes are grouped into API/documentation updates, database/schema changes, new service logic, and operational guidance.

**Key changes:**

### API and Documentation Enhancements

* Extended the API documentation (`API_DOCUMENTATION.md`) to describe new endpoints for consumables forecasting, including settings updates, forecast retrieval, and paper refill actions, with validation rules and example payloads. 
* Added operational instructions for setting up Epson L5290 ink telemetry and using the new consumables forecasting features.

### Database and Schema Updates

* Introduced new interfaces and default settings for `consumablesForecasting` within the application settings schema (`db.ts`), including normalization and validation logic. 
* Added new SQLite tables for `consumable_usage_events` (tracks paper usage) and `consumable_ink_snapshots` (tracks ink telemetry), with supporting TypeScript interfaces and migration logic.

### Service and Logic Implementation

* Implemented a new `ConsumablesSqliteStore` class to handle reading and writing consumables usage and ink snapshot data in SQLite, including methods for appending and listing events.
* Updated the admin controller to integrate a new `ConsumablesService` for handling consumables-related API routes and logic.

### Design and Specification

* Added a detailed design document outlining the architecture, data model, forecasting algorithms, API surface, UI considerations, error handling, and rollout plan for the consumables forecasting feature.

---

These changes lay the foundation for proactive consumables management, making it easier for admins to anticipate and address low paper or ink before service interruptions occur.

author: andrii-rohovyi
body:
### Summary
                                                                                                                                                                       
  Implement the Early Pruning optimization that reduces RAPTOR query time by breaking out of transfer iteration early when remaining (sorted) transfers cannot improve the solution. Following the discussion with @t2gran during the OTP meeting on April 7, 2026, this PR is submitted for review. 
                                                                                                                                                                       
  ### Issue       

  Closes #7470                                                                                                                                                         
   
  ### Unit tests                                                                                                                                                       
                  
  - All existing OTP unit tests pass with the change.
  - No new unit tests were added — the optimization is a performance improvement that preserves identical routing results.
  - Manual verification: benchmarked on 1,000 random queries in the Norway (Oslo region) graph across 30/60/90 min max transfer durations. Results are 100% identical to baseline (0 differences in paths found).                                                                                                                          
  - Performance improvement: +8.5% at 30 min, +8.2% at 60 min, +10.4% at 90 min transfer duration.                                                                     
  - No regression on the standard OTP Norway SpeedTest (45 test cases, identical path counts).                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                       
  ### Documentation                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                       
  - Design and rationale documented in code comments, referencing the paper: Rohovyi, Abuaisha, Walsh — "Early Pruning for Public Transport Routing", accepted at WCTR 2026 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.12592).
  - The optimization can be toggled via system property `otp.raptor.earlyPruning` (enabled by default, set to `"false"` to disable).                                   
  - No new user-facing configuration options were added.

body: ## 优化概述（C8 阶段） 在前序 C1~C7 阶段（1x1/3x3/5x5 grouped conv 等热点优化）基础上，本 PR 针对三个关键卷积路径实施系统性**空间分块（spatial tiling）**优化，进一步降低 MobileNet 推理周期 20.4%。 ### 核心改动 #### 1. `Conv2D_1x1` 4-pixel 空间分块（`conv.cc`） - **问题**：OC 向量化路径下，每个 `out_x` 像素独立处理，权重向量被重复加载 N 次（N = output_width）。 - **优化**：内层 `out_x` 循环改为 4-pixel tile，每次权重加载同时驱动 4 个累加器（4 个相邻像素位置），**权重加载次数减少 75%**。 - **边界处理**：检测 `in_x0 < 0 || in_x3 >= input_width`，不满足时回落 scalar 路径，保持正确性。 #### 2. `Conv2D_3x3` 4-pixel 空间分块（`conv.cc`） - **问题**：3x3 kernel 下，每个像素位置的 9 个 filter tap 每次都被重新读取。 - **优化**：在 `dilation==1` 快路径中，同时处理 4 个相邻 `out_x` 位置，9 个 filter tap vector load 被 4 个像素共享，**filter 加载摊销 4 倍**。 - **边界/dilation!=1**：自动回落到逐像素 scalar 路径。 #### 3. `DepthwiseConvPerChannelPatchCenter5x5Preload`（`depthwise_conv.cc`） - **问题**：DepthwiseConv 5x5 中心区域走通用 `Patch` 路径，每个输出位置重复计算 25 个 filter tap 的地址偏移。 - **优化**：新增专用中心区域内核，使用直接指针运算预计算 filter tap 地址，消除每像素的重复地址计算开销。接入 `DepthwiseConvPerChannel` 分发树（`stride_w == dilation_w` 条件）。 ### 性能数据 | Workload | C7 基线 | C8 结果 | 变化 | |---|---|---|---| | npusim_mobilenet | 40,017,353 | 31,840,506 | **-20.4%** | | npusim_bcresnet | 254,702,861 | 254,941,208 | +0.09%（噪声范围内） | **累积改善（相对 A 阶段基线 mobilenet=516,177,367）：-93.8%** ### 验证矩阵（全量通过） | 测试 | 结果 | |---|---| | `//sw/opt/litert-micro/test:conv_sim_test` | ✅ PASS | | `//tests/cocotb:rvv_ml_ops_cocotb_test` | ✅ PASS | | `//tests/cocotb:rvv_arithmetic_cocotb_test` | ✅ PASS | | `//tests/cocotb:rvv_load_store_test` | ✅ PASS | | `//tests/cocotb:rvv_highmem_tests` | ✅ PASS | | `//tests/cocotb:rvv_itcm512kb_dtcm512kb_tests` | ✅ PASS | | `npusim_run_mobilenet` | ✅ PASS (cycles=31,840,506) | | `npusim_run_bcresnet` | ✅ PASS (cycles=254,941,208) |

cobalt: Fix crashpad handler launch on ATV

Modify Crashpad's GetHandlerTrampoline and LaunchAtCrashHandler
to support direct ELF execution of the handler from APK offsets
using the system linker. This resolves an issue where the crashpad
handler failed to launch from an uncompressed binary within the APK
on Cobalt Android TV. On ATV, the handler's main entry point is
expected directly from its shared object, not the main Cobalt SO.

Additionally, add "Freeze detection" lifecycle logs to the reporting
chain, wrapped in IS_COBALT build flags. These logs aid in debugging
crashpad handler initialization and reporting, especially for freeze
events, on Cobalt.

Bug: 484122527

author: i-am-nothing
body:
## Summary

Adds the per-Module event subscription, emit declaration, and cron registration APIs the issue calls for. Handlers auto-mount on the Internal scope (gated by `InternalAuth` from #36) at deterministic paths the platform's event bus and scheduler can derive without guessing.

## API surface

All panic on duplicate or invalid name. Call from startup code, not request handlers.

```go
// Subscribe to an event from another module — handler mounted at
// /events/{name}, recorded in manifest.events.subscribes.
mod.OnEvent("oauth.user_deleted", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { ... })

// Declare an emitted event — appears in manifest.events.emits.
mod.Emit("created")

// Register a cron job — handler mounted at /crons/{name}, recorded
// in manifest.schedules with cron string + path.
mod.Cron("cleanup-temp", "0 3 * * *", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { ... })
```

Top-level wrappers (`ms.OnEvent`, `ms.Emit`, `ms.Cron`) dispatch through `mustDefault`, panic before `Init()` — matches the existing `Platform`/`Public`/`Internal`/`RequirePermission` pattern.

## Registry changes

- `Schedule` struct gains a `Path` field so the platform's scheduler knows the URL to invoke. `AddSchedule` signature broadens from `(name, cron)` to `(name, cron, path)`. All callers updated.
- New `HasSubscribe` / `HasEmit` / `HasSchedule` helpers — lock-free read-locked existence checks so the user-facing API can panic on duplicates without deep-cloning the whole map/slice.

## Security

`validateRegistrationName` rejects empty names, path separators (`/`, `\`), dot-segments (`..`), and whitespace. Without this check, `OnEvent(\"../admin\", h)` would let chi normalize the registered pattern to `/admin`, silently escaping the `/events/` namespace AND making the manifest payload disagree with the actual mounted route.

This was the **MEDIUM finding** from the security/efficiency `/simplify` review:

> The platform-vs-chi disagreement is the real bug: events fired at \`/events/../admin\` by the platform hit a 404, while a separate \`Platform()\` route at \`/admin\` actually receives them.

`TestOnEvent_PanicsOnPathInjection`, `TestEmit_PanicsOnPathInjection`, and `TestCron_PanicsOnPathInjection` are the regression guards (covering 6 attack patterns: empty, `../`, `/`, `\`, space, newline).

## Test coverage

- Handler reachability via internal scope (200 with secret, 401 without)
- Manifest serialization (`subscribes` / `emits` / `schedules`)
- Duplicate registration panic
- Empty / path-injection name panic (security regression)
- Top-level wrapper panic-before-Init (added to `TestScopesPanic_BeforeInit`)
- Two-module isolation guarantee (m1's manifest does not see m2's events)
- Empty schedule string panic (cron-specific)
- New `Has*` helpers (`TestHasSubscribe_HasEmit_HasSchedule`)

## Reviews applied (`/simplify`)

3 review agents (reuse / quality / security+efficiency). Findings addressed:

| Severity | Finding | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **MED** | S1: Path injection via event/cron name | **Fixed** — `validateRegistrationName` + 6-case regression test |
| **MED** | Empty name validation gap on `OnEvent`/`Emit` | **Fixed** — same helper handles all three |
| Medium | Reuse #4: `/events/` and `/crons/` hardcoded literals | **Fixed** — `eventPathPrefix` / `cronPathPrefix` constants |
| Quality | Panic message verb consistency (\"declared\" vs \"registered\") | **Fixed** — all use \"registered twice\" |
| Quality | `TestModulesIsolated_Cron` redundant with `TestModulesIsolated_OnEvent` | **Fixed** — dropped, replaced with cross-reference comment |
| Quality | WHAT-narration in doc comments | **Fixed** — trimmed `OnEvent` chi-dot paragraph and `Emit` TBD paragraph |

## Out-of-scope follow-ups

Will file separate issues:

- **Event/cron name enumeration via 401 vs 404** — related to #44 but more impactful because event names follow predictable conventions (`module.action`). An unauthenticated attacker can map a deployed module's full subscription surface without ever guessing the secret.
- **Manifest contract doc update** — `docs/module-protocol.md` needs the `schedules[].path` field added to its example. Parent repo, separate PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `go test -race ./...` all packages green
- [x] Path injection: `TestOnEvent_PanicsOnPathInjection`, `TestEmit_PanicsOnPathInjection`, `TestCron_PanicsOnPathInjection`
- [x] Two-module isolation: `TestModulesIsolated_OnEvent`
- [x] Manifest serialization: `TestOnEvent_AppearsInManifestSubscribes`, `TestEmit_AppearsInManifestEmits`, `TestCron_AppearsInManifestSchedules`
- [x] Internal-secret gating: `TestOnEvent_RequiresInternalSecret`, `TestCron_RequiresInternalSecret`

Closes #9

This PR updates [pytest](https://pypi.org/project/pytest) from **4.1.1** to **9.0.3**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 9.0.3
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `12444 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12444>`_: Fixed :func:`pytest.approx` which now correctly takes into account :class:`~collections.abc.Mapping` keys order to compare them.


- `13634 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13634>`_: Blocking a ``conftest.py`` file using the ``-p no:`` option is now explicitly disallowed.

  Previously this resulted in an internal assertion failure during plugin loading.

  Pytest now raises a clear ``UsageError`` explaining that conftest files are not plugins and cannot be disabled via ``-p``.


- `13734 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13734>`_: Fixed crash when a test raises an exceptiongroup with ``__tracebackhide__ = True``.


- `14195 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14195>`_: Fixed an issue where non-string messages passed to `unittest.TestCase.subTest()` were not printed.


- `14343 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14343>`_: Fixed use of insecure temporary directory (CVE-2025-71176).



Improved documentation
----------------------

- `13388 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13388>`_: Clarified documentation for ``-p`` vs ``PYTEST_PLUGINS`` plugin loading and fixed an incorrect ``-p`` example.


- `13731 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13731>`_: Clarified that capture fixtures (e.g. ``capsys`` and ``capfd``) take precedence over the ``-s`` / ``--capture=no`` command-line options in :ref:`Accessing captured output from a test function <accessing-captured-output>`.


- `14088 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14088>`_: Clarified that the default :hook:`pytest_collection` hook sets ``session.items`` before it calls :hook:`pytest_collection_finish`, not after.


- `14255 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14255>`_: TOML integer log levels must be quoted: Updating reference documentation.



Contributor-facing changes
--------------------------

- `12689 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12689>`_: The test reports are now published to Codecov from GitHub Actions.
  The test statistics is visible `on the web interface
  <https://app.codecov.io/gh/pytest-dev/pytest/tests>`__.

  -- by :user:`aleguy02`
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.0.2
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `13896 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13896>`_: The terminal progress feature added in pytest 9.0.0 has been disabled by default, except on Windows, due to compatibility issues with some terminal emulators.

  You may enable it again by passing ``-p terminalprogress``. We may enable it by default again once compatibility improves in the future.

  Additionally, when the environment variable ``TERM`` is ``dumb``, the escape codes are no longer emitted, even if the plugin is enabled.


- `13904 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13904>`_: Fixed the TOML type of the :confval:`tmp_path_retention_count` settings in the API reference from number to string.


- `13946 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13946>`_: The private ``config.inicfg`` attribute was changed in a breaking manner in pytest 9.0.0.

   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `13895 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13895>`_: Restore support for skipping tests via ``raise unittest.SkipTest``.


- `13896 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13896>`_: The terminal progress plugin added in pytest 9.0 is now automatically disabled when iTerm2 is detected, it generated desktop notifications instead of the desired functionality.


- `13904 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13904>`_: Fixed the TOML type of the verbosity settings in the API reference from number to string.


- `13910 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13910>`_: Fixed `UserWarning: Do not expect file_or_dir` on some earlier Python 3.12 and 3.13 point versions.



Packaging updates and notes for downstreams
-------------------------------------------

- `13933 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13933>`_: The tox configuration has been adjusted to make sure the desired
  version string can be passed into its :ref:`package_env` through
  the ``SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST`` environment
  variable as a part of the release process -- by :user:`webknjaz`.



Contributor-facing changes
--------------------------

- `13891 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13891>`_, `#13942 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13942>`_: The CI/CD part of the release automation is now capable of
  creating GitHub Releases without having a Git checkout on
  disk -- by :user:`bluetech` and :user:`webknjaz`.


- `13933 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13933>`_: The tox configuration has been adjusted to make sure the desired
  version string can be passed into its :ref:`package_env` through
  the ``SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST`` environment
  variable as a part of the release process -- by :user:`webknjaz`.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.0.0
   ```
   =========================

New features
------------


- `1367 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1367>`_: **Support for subtests** has been added.

  :ref:`subtests <subtests>` are an alternative to parametrization, useful in situations where the parametrization values are not all known at collection time.

  Example:

  .. code-block:: python

      def contains_docstring(p: Path) -> bool:
          """Return True if the given Python file contains a top-level docstring."""
          ...


      def test_py_files_contain_docstring(subtests: pytest.Subtests) -> None:
          for path in Path.cwd().glob("*.py"):
              with subtests.test(path=str(path)):
                  assert contains_docstring(path)


  Each assert failure or error is caught by the context manager and reported individually, giving a clear picture of all files that are missing a docstring.

  In addition, :meth:`unittest.TestCase.subTest` is now also supported.

  This feature was originally implemented as a separate plugin in `pytest-subtests <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-subtests>`__, but since then has been merged into the core.

  .. note::

      This feature is experimental and will likely evolve in future releases. By that we mean that we might change how subtests are reported on failure, but the functionality and how to use it are stable.


- `13743 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13743>`_: Added support for **native TOML configuration files**.

  While pytest, since version 6, supports configuration in ``pyproject.toml`` files under ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]``,
  it does so in an "INI compatibility mode", where all configuration values are treated as strings or list of strings.
  Now, pytest supports the native TOML data model.

  In ``pyproject.toml``, the native TOML configuration is under the ``[tool.pytest]`` table.

  .. code-block:: toml

       pyproject.toml
      [tool.pytest]
      minver

author: biboylin
body:
## Summary

This PR improves the device UI update path so on-screen status text better matches the real runtime state, while also addressing stability issues discovered during desktop expression testing.

## What changed

- Make `font_size` actually take effect in the display layer
  - English / ASCII status text now maps to real LVGL Montserrat fonts
  - CJK / mixed text continues to use `SimSun 16 CJK`
  - Enabled required LVGL font configs for Montserrat 20 / 22 / 24

- Fix stale text remaining on screen when switching into empty-text states
  - Empty strings now explicitly clear the label
  - States like `standby`, `speaking`, `happy`, `bluetooth`, and `custom3` no longer inherit the previous message

- Improve display refresh semantics
  - `display_ui` now treats font size and text style as part of the rendered state
  - Prevents false no-op updates when text is unchanged but style/size changed

- Remove behavior/LVGL lock nesting from the state service
  - Behavior state updates now build a display request while holding the behavior lock
  - Actual display calls happen after unlocking
  - Reduces the chance of the main loop being blocked behind LVGL work

- Harden behavior status queries used by the main loop
  - `behavior_state_is_busy()` and `behavior_state_is_action_active()` now use bounded lock waits
  - On timeout they fail safe as busy, which avoids idle-hint UI churn during transient contention
  - Timeout logs are rate-limited

- Increase WebSocket client task stack headroom
  - Helps avoid the `websocket_task` stack overflow seen after cloud session startup

## Why

Before this change, UI status rendering had two main problems:

1. Requested font sizes were mostly nominal and did not actually change the rendered font.
2. States with empty default text often left the previous status text visible, causing the UI to drift from the device’s actual behavior.

During validation, additional runtime issues also appeared:
- behavior lock / LVGL lock contention
- repeated idle-hint interference during transient lock timeouts
- `websocket_task` stack overflow after session ready

This PR addresses those issues together so the UI is both more accurate and more robust.

## Validation

- ESP-IDF build passes successfully
- Firmware flashed and tested on `COM28`
- Verified boot, Wi-Fi, discovery, and WebSocket ready flow
- Verified status text clearing and real font-size application path
- Verified the previous immediate `websocket_task` stack-overflow reboot no longer reproduces in startup validation

## Notes

- Resource-name typo aliasing in `control_ingress` was intentionally reverted and is not part of this PR
- Frontend / desktop panel should continue to send the exact resource IDs it wants the firmware to use

## Summary
Countdown to next prayer was using device's local timezone instead of the selected location's timezone. For example, Istanbul showing "7h 11m to Sunrise" when Sunrise was actually 12 minutes away.

### Root cause
`DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day, hour, minute)` creates a DateTime in the device's local timezone, but `now` is a TZDateTime in the location's timezone. The difference calculation was comparing UTC timestamps across different zones.

### Fix
Added `TimezoneUtil.timeAt()` to create target DateTime in the correct timezone.

- [ ] Set location to local — still works correctly

author: koheikameyama
body:
## Summary

Implements a liquidity check filter that validates order book depth and spread before executing entry orders. This prevents slippage and execution failures on thinly-traded stocks by checking best ask/bid prices and quantities in real-time.

## Key Changes

- **New `checkLiquidity()` function** in `src/core/market-data.ts`
  - Validates spread percentage against `MAX_SPREAD_PCT` (0.5%)
  - Checks ask-side board depth against order quantity with `MIN_BOARD_DEPTH_RATIO` (1.0x)
  - Flags high sell pressure when `askSize / bidSize >= SELL_PRESSURE_THRESHOLD` (3.0)
  - Returns structured `LiquidityCheckResult` with pass/fail status, spread %, and risk flags
  - Gracefully handles missing quote data (yfinance fallback) by passing through

- **Integration into entry execution** in `src/core/breakout/entry-executor.ts`
  - Fetches fresh stock quote immediately before broker order submission
  - Runs liquidity check after risk validation but before order placement
  - Blocks entry with `retryable: true` if spread or board depth fails (allows retry on next scan)
  - Logs risk flags as warnings without blocking (e.g., "sell pressure high")
  - Records liquidity snapshot (`askPrice`, `bidPrice`, `askSize`, `bidSize`, `spreadPct`) in `entrySnapshot` for post-trade analysis

- **New constants** in `src/lib/constants/trading.ts`
  - Introduced `LIQUIDITY_FILTER` with three configurable thresholds
  - Deprecated `SPREAD_FILTER` in favor of `LIQUIDITY_FILTER.MAX_SPREAD_PCT`

- **Documentation update** in `docs/specs/trading-architecture.md`
  - Moved liquidity filter from "future phases" to active implementation
  - Clarified judgment logic with specific thresholds and formulas
  - Documented fallback behavior when board data unavailable
  - Listed future enhancements (board volatility, multi-level depth, exit-side checks)

## Implementation Details

- Liquidity check is **non-blocking for warnings**: sell pressure flags are logged but don't prevent execution
- **Retryable failures** (spread/depth) allow the order to be re-evaluated on the next market scan
- **Quote data is optional**: if `askPrice`/`bidPrice` are unavailable, the check passes (maintains backward compatibility with data sources that don't provide order book info)
- Spread calculation uses mid-price: `(askPrice - bidPrice) / price * 100`
- Board depth check is relative to order quantity: `askSize >= orderQuantity * MIN_BOARD_DEPTH_RATIO`

body:
## One-Line Summary
Adds a repo-local OneQuery plugin bundle that Claude Code and Codex can install to discover sources, manage explicit local CLI state, connect sources, and run guided read-only query workflows.

## User-Facing Changes
- Adds a shared `plugins/onequery` bundle with plugin manifests for both Claude Code and Codex.
- Registers `onequery` in the repo-local marketplace so Codex can install it from `/plugins` during local development.
- Adds skill docs for safe discovery, read-only querying, explicit-only local state changes, and explicit-only source connection flows.
- Documents local install and reload steps in the plugin README.

## Why This Changed
Before this change, the repository did not package the existing OneQuery CLI into an installable agent plugin, so local agent workflows depended on ad hoc prompting and manual command discovery.

body:
## Summary
- allow binding `matches` conditions in `if`, `elif`, and ternary expressions by lowering conditional `matches` arms directly to nested `match` expressions
- update `Declaration` scope bookkeeping so conditional-match binders are visible only in the corresponding `matches` guard and true arm
- preserve outer condition annotations for conditional `matches`, keeping bad annotated conditions as type errors
- add parser, source-converter, scope, error-message, evaluation, and totality regressions plus language-guide coverage

## Why
Conditional `matches` forms already parse, but binding patterns were rejected during source conversion and their binders were not scoped correctly in `Declaration` traversals. That prevented code like `if foo matches Some(a): fn(a)` from lowering with the same semantics as an explicit nested `match`.

## Impact
Conditional `matches` now behave like explicit `match` desugarings, including guarded forms and mixed boolean / `matches` chains, without changing standalone `matches` semantics outside conditional position.

author: scottm5443
body:
The Alarm.com API requires a non-zero duration when setting fan mode to ON (the app shows "On 1 hr", "On 3 hrs", "On 24 hrs"). Sending `desiredFanDuration=0` with ON mode was silently ignored by the API, so the fan mode appeared to accept the change but nothing happened.

**Fix:** For ON mode, read `supported_fan_durations` from the device and use the longest available duration (typically 1440 min = 24 hr). AUTO and CIRCULATE modes don't use a duration at all, so `desiredFanDuration` is now omitted for those modes.

author: andrew-jayne
body:
So I was working on a project at work and I wanted to use botocore's ARN utilities for a validation workflow. basically I needed a type I could use in Pydantic models that would blow up on construction if the value wasn't a valid ARN.

When I looked at the ArnParser class, I noticed a couple of things:

parse_arn was too permissive — it accepted any 6-part colon-delimited string. So passing a garbage string wouldn't raise, even though the intent of parse_arn (vs. is_arn) feels like it should be the strict path. I tightened the validation to check the arn prefix, partition (aws*), non-empty service, region format, 12-digit account ID, and non-empty resource.

self was unused in parse_arn  so it moved it to a @staticmethod so you don't need to instantiate ArnParser just to parse an ARN. Instantiation still works for backwards compat.

ArnStr is just a simple a str subclass (following the same pattern as ServiceId) that validates on construction. Useful as a type annotation anywhere you want the runtime guarantee that a string that is supposed to be an ARN is actually a valid ARN.

I updated the existing tests and added a few new test cases for the validation paths and ArnStr.

Let me know if you want any changes or if this just does not fit boto core, happy to make any tweaks.

-AJ

author: 7etsuo
body:
## Summary

Phase B of the 16-phase refactor in [`TODO.MD`](../blob/main/TODO.MD). Replaces the serial `for` loop at `chat-executor-tool-loop.ts:1052` with partition-aware batch dispatch. Consecutive concurrency-safe tool calls now run in parallel via `Promise.all`; every other call runs serially. Mirrors `claude_code/services/tools/toolOrchestration.ts:152-177`.

Before this PR, `isConcurrencySafe` was **telemetry-only** — the honest scorecard in TODO.MD marked "Parallel tool dispatch" as **TELEMETRY ONLY** because the loop iterated serially even when a batch of read-only tools could have been dispatched at once. That status is now closed.

## Files touched

- **`runtime/src/llm/chat-executor-tool-loop.ts`** — replace the serial dispatch with per-batch dispatch. Safe batches with length > 1 use `Promise.all(batch.toolCalls.map(executeSingleToolCall))`; safe batches with length 1 and unsafe batches fall back to the serial inner loop. All action results per batch are collected; the round breaks on any `end_round` / `abort_loop` / `abort_round`. The pre-existing `tool_dispatch_started` trace and the dispatch path now share one `partitionToolCalls()` call.
- **`runtime/src/llm/chat-executor-parallel-dispatch.test.ts`** *(new)* — 3 tests covering the hot paths:
  1. 3 concurrency-safe calls against a slow mock handler complete in < 2× the per-call sleep (parallel proof) and have a start-time spread < SLEEP_MS/2 (overlap proof). Serial would be ~3× and ~2× respectively.
  2. `isConcurrencySafe: () => false` forces serial dispatch (~3× sleep, ~2× spread).
  3. Omitting `isConcurrencySafe` keeps the default serial path (~2× sleep for 2 calls).
  All three use `system.readFile` to stay clear of the turn-execution contract mutation policy.
- **`docs/REFACTOR-LOG.md`** — record U1 Phase A (PR #261) in the ledger.

## Concurrency safety notes

- **Result ordering**: the `tool_result` protocol does not require results to appear in the same order as their originating tool_calls — each tool_result carries a `tool_call_id` the provider matches against the prior assistant message. Completion order is therefore acceptable, which is what `Promise.all` gives us.
- **Ctx mutations**: JavaScript is single-threaded, so per-call mutations (messages, allToolCalls, trace events) are atomic between await points.
- **Image-char budget**: `loopState.remainingToolImageChars` has a theoretical read-modify-write race across interleaved parallel calls, but tools in the concurrency-safe allowlist are read-only (`system.readFile`, `system.listDir`, etc.) and do not return images, so the drift is bounded to zero in practice. A hard fix would split `executeSingleToolCall` into execute/commit phases; that's deferred to Phase F's class deletion pass.

## Verification

```
node runtime/scripts/check-executor-baseline.mjs
  test file count 359 >= 357 (up from 358)
  it()/test() block count 5986 >= 5976 (up from 5983)
  baseline OK (20ms)

npm run typecheck --workspace=@tetsuo-ai/runtime: clean

vitest runtime/src/llm/chat-executor-parallel-dispatch.test.ts: 3/3
vitest runtime/src/llm/chat-executor.test.ts: 107/107 (no regression)
vitest runtime/src/llm/ (full module): 423/423 across 26 files

Full runtime test suite: 6048/6048 production tests pass, 5 expected
conditional skips. One pre-existing LiteSVM setup failure in
tests/marketplace-cli.integration.test.ts — reproduces on main, not
caused by this PR.
```

## Phase

U2 (Phase B) of the 16-phase executor refactor. Unblocks U3 (Phase D: streaming event types).

### Motivation

- The app was failing to boot in newer Python runtimes because some pinned scientific packages and transitive `pillow` were being built from source and failing due to missing system libraries (e.g., `zlib`).
- The goal is to avoid source builds on Python 3.13+ by selecting wheel-friendly package ranges while preserving existing Python 3.11 pins.

### Description

- Updated `requirements.txt` to add Python-version-aware constraints for `numpy`, `pandas`, and `matplotlib` so older pins remain for Python 3.11 and relaxed wheel-friendly ranges apply for Python >= 3.13.
- Added an explicit `pillow>=11,<12` requirement so modern runtimes pick prebuilt wheels and avoid `zlib` compile failures when building from source.
- Added a short note to `README.md` explaining why the version markers were introduced and how they help on Python 3.14+ deployments.

Nuevo flujo de scraping sin login directo del usuario, con soporte de ejecución por jobs y runner dedicado para Apify.
Ajustes en persistencia y modelos de scraping para PostgreSQL, incluyendo cambios de esquema y migraciones.
Actualización del worker y configuración de despliegue para soportar el nuevo modo de ejecución de scraping.
Ampliación de payloads y metadata para generación de reportes/estrategias con OpenAI.
Incorporación de un blog público estático con parsing de markdown, SEO, prerender y componentes dedicados.
Mejora del manejo de errores HTTP en frontend con pantallas específicas para 403, 404, 500 y 503.
Refuerzo de navegación/autenticación en rutas protegidas y redirecciones a login.
Nuevas pruebas backend y frontend para scraping, persistencia, errores HTTP, sesión, blog y login.
Impacto técnico

Backend: nuevas rutas, servicios, migraciones, tests y soporte de ejecución de scraping vía worker.
Frontend: nuevas rutas públicas, componentes de blog, parsing seguro de markdown, SEO y pruebas E2E/unitarias.
Infra: cambios en Dockerfile, fly.*.toml, variables de entorno y locks de dependencias.
