*April 7, 2026*

Django 6.0.4 fixes one security issue with severity "moderate", four security
issues with severity "low", and several bugs in 6.0.3.

CVE-2026-3902: ASGI header spoofing via underscore/hyphen conflation
====================================================================

``ASGIRequest`` normalizes header names following WSGI conventions, mapping
hyphens to underscores. As a result, even in configurations where reverse
proxies carefully strip security-sensitive headers named with hyphens, such a
header could be spoofed by supplying a header named with underscores.

Under WSGI, it is the responsibility of the server or proxy to avoid ambiguous
mappings. (Django's :djadmin:`runserver` was patched in :cve:`2015-0219`.) But
under ASGI, there is not the same uniform expectation, even if many proxies
protect against this under default configuration (including ``nginx`` via
``underscores_in_headers off;``).

Headers containing underscores are now ignored by ``ASGIRequest``, matching the
behavior of :pypi:`Daphne <daphne>`, the reference server for ASGI.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-4277: Privilege abuse in ``GenericInlineModelAdmin``
=============================================================

Add permissions on inline model instances were not validated on submission of
forged ``POST`` data in
:class:`~django.contrib.contenttypes.admin.GenericInlineModelAdmin`.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-4292: Privilege abuse in ``ModelAdmin.list_editable``
==============================================================

Admin changelist forms using
:attr:`~django.contrib.admin.ModelAdmin.list_editable` incorrectly allowed new
instances to be created via forged ``POST`` data.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-33033: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ``MultiPartParser`` via base64-encoded file upload
===============================================================================================================

When using ``django.http.multipartparser.MultiPartParser``, multipart uploads
with ``Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64`` that include excessive whitespace
may trigger repeated memory copying, potentially degrading performance.

This issue has severity "moderate" according to the :ref:`Django security
policy <security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-33034: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ASGI requests via memory upload limit bypass
=========================================================================================================

ASGI requests with a missing or understated ``Content-Length`` header could
bypass the :setting:`DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE` limit when reading
``HttpRequest.body``, potentially loading an unbounded request body into
memory and causing service degradation.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a regression in Django 6.0 where :func:`~django.contrib.auth.alogin`
  and :func:`~django.contrib.auth.alogout` did not respectively set or clear
  ``request.user`` if it had already been materialized (e.g., by sync
  middleware) (:ticket:`37017`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 6.0 in admin forms where
  ``RelatedFieldWidgetWrapper`` incorrectly wrapped all widgets in a
  ``<fieldset>`` (:ticket:`36949`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 6.0 where the ``fields.E348`` system check did not
  detect name clashes between model managers and
  :attr:`~django.db.models.ForeignKey.related_name`\s for non-self-referential
  relationships (:ticket:`36973`).


==========================
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0.3
   ```
   ==========================

*March 3, 2026*

Django 6.0.3 fixes a security issue with severity "moderate", a security issue
with severity "low", and several bugs in 6.0.2.

CVE-2026-25673: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ``URLField`` via Unicode normalization on Windows
==============================================================================================================

The :class:`~django.forms.URLField` form field's ``to_python()`` method used
:func:`~urllib.parse.urlsplit` to determine whether to prepend a URL scheme to
the submitted value. On Windows, ``urlsplit()`` performs
:func:`NFKC normalization <python:unicodedata.normalize>`, which can be
disproportionately slow for large inputs containing certain characters.

``URLField.to_python()`` now uses a simplified scheme detection, avoiding
Unicode normalization entirely and deferring URL validation to the appropriate
layers. As a result, while leading and trailing whitespace is still stripped by
default, characters such as newlines, tabs, and other control characters within
the value are no longer handled by ``URLField.to_python()``. When using the
default :class:`~django.core.validators.URLValidator`, these values will
continue to raise :exc:`~django.core.exceptions.ValidationError` during
validation, but if you rely on custom validators, ensure they do not depend on
the previous behavior of ``URLField.to_python()``.

This issue has severity "moderate" according to the :ref:`Django security
policy <security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-25674: Potential incorrect permissions on newly created file system objects
====================================================================================

Django's file-system storage and file-based cache backends used the process
``umask`` to control permissions when creating directories. In multi-threaded
environments, one thread's temporary umask change can affect other threads'
file and directory creation, resulting in file system objects being created
with unintended permissions.

Django now applies the requested permissions via :func:`~os.chmod` after
:func:`~os.mkdir`, removing the dependency on the process-wide umask.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

Bugfixes

* Fixed :exc:`NameError` when inspecting functions making use of deferred
  annotations in Python 3.14 (:ticket:`36903`).

* Fixed :exc:`AttributeError` when subclassing builtin lookups and neglecting
  to :ref:`override<tuple-for-params>` ``as_sql()`` to accept any sequence

* Fixed :exc:`TypeError` when deprecation warnings are emitted in environments

* Fixed a visual regression where fieldset legends were misaligned in the admin

* Prevented the :data:`django.tasks.signals.task_finished` signal from writing

author: vahid-sohrabloo
body:
When a batch node has exactly 1 key assigned to it, several batch command types fall back to `executeSingle` which
   incorrectly iterates **all records/keys** in the entire batch instead of only the record(s) assigned to the current node
    via `cmd.batch.offsets`.

   This causes N sequential `client.Operate` round trips instead of 1, where N is the total number of keys in the batch.

   ### Impact

   On cross-datacenter connections with ~2.5ms RTT, a `BatchGetComplex` with 10 keys takes **~25ms instead of ~3ms**
   because `executeSingle` sends 10 individual Operate calls sequentially.

   ### Root cause

   Compare the **correct** implementation in `batchCommandGet.executeSingle`:

   ```go
   // Correct: iterates only this node's assigned keys
   for _, offset := range cmd.batch.offsets {
       cmd.records[offset], err = client.Get(...)
   }
   ```

   With the **buggy** implementation in `batchIndexCommandGet.executeSingle`:

   ```go
   // Bug: iterates ALL records in the batch
   for _, br := range cmd.records {
       client.Operate(...)
   }
   ```

   ### Affected files

   | File | Execute condition | Loop iterates | Bug |
   |------|------------------|---------------|-----|
   | `batch_command_get.go` | `len(cmd.batch.offsets) == 1` | `cmd.batch.offsets` | ✅ Correct |
   | `batch_command_exists.go` | `len(cmd.batch.offsets) == 1` | `cmd.batch.offsets` | ✅ Correct |
   | `batch_index_command_get.go` | `len(cmd.batch.offsets) == 1` | `cmd.records` | ❌ Bug |
   | `batch_command_operate.go` | `len(cmd.records) == 1` | `cmd.records` | ❌ Bug |
   | `batch_command_delete.go` | `len(cmd.keys) == 1` | `cmd.keys` | ❌ Bug |
   | `batch_command_udf.go` | `len(cmd.keys) == 1` | `cmd.keys` | ❌ Bug |

   ### Fix

   For all affected files:
   1. Check `len(cmd.batch.offsets) == 1` instead of `len(cmd.records/keys) == 1`
   2. Iterate `cmd.batch.offsets` and index into `cmd.records/keys` by offset

   ### Reproduction

   Test against a 3-node cluster with metrics enabled:

   ```go
   client.EnableMetrics(aero.DefaultMetricsPolicy())
   _, _ = client.Stats() // reset

   for range 100 {
       reads := make([]*aero.BatchRead, 10)
       for i := range 10 {
           reads[i] = aero.NewBatchRead(nil, keys[i], []string{"val"})
       }
       client.BatchGetComplex(bp, reads)
   }

   stats, _ := client.Stats()
   // Check operate-metrics count in cluster-aggregated-stats
   // Expected: 0 (all should use batch protocol)
   // Actual: 1000 (10 Operate calls per iteration)

### Motivation

- Implement an end-to-end monitor run orchestration to execute `query_task` searches, generate LLM summaries and deliver cards to Feishu. 
- Encapsulate external integrations (PubMed, LLM, Feishu) behind small, testable adapters and services. 
- Introduce a repository layer and lightweight `SQLiteAdapter` to centralize persistence and support future adapter swaps. 
- Provide a simple manual runner and documentation to make the new flow immediately usable and reviewable.

### Description

- Added a monitor agent package with `MonitorRunService`, `MonitorRunHandler`, structured runtime schemas (`MonitorRunResult`, `PaperProcessResult`, `RunOutcome`) and `MonitorEventLogger`. 
- Implemented integrations: PubMed (`search_client`, `fetch_client`, `mapper`, `service`), LLM (`client`, `prompt_builder`, `service`, `schemas`) and Feishu (`card_builder`, `client`, `schemas`). 
- Introduced repository layer and helpers: `DatabaseAdapter` / `SQLiteAdapter`, repositories for `QueryTask`, `MonitorRun`, `Paper`/`PaperQueryHit`, `LlmSummary`, `DeliveryRecord`, `Feedback`, `PreferenceProfile`, plus common utils and exceptions. 
- Added DB initialization script `db/init_db.py`, a manual runner `scripts/run_monitor_once.py`, documentation (`docs/*`) describing contracts and flow, and unit tests for integrations, service orchestration and repositories (`tests/test_integrations.py`, `tests/test_monitor_run_service.py`, `tests/test_repositories.py`).

### Testing

- Ran `tests/test_integrations.py` which validates PubMed mapping, LLM service mapping and Feishu card payload generation, and it passed.

However, when starting the server via: ``` sglang serve --model-path /data/Qwen-Image-Layered --host 0.0.0.0 --port 12500 ``` And sending a request to the /v1/images/edits endpoint: ``` curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:12500/v1/images/edits \ -F "image=@/data/qwen-image-layered/4.png" \ -F "num_frames=4" ``` The server raises an error indicating that the prompt field is required, even though the model does not necessarily need a text prompt for this task. The endpoint should either make prompt optional or provide a sensible default value. 2.When the server processes the output and attempts to save an image with an RGBA color mode, it tries to save the file in JPEG format, which does not support transparency (alpha channel). This causes an error. In the `sglang generate` case, the `DataType.get_default_extension` logic is used, where the default extension for images is PNG. In the `sglang serve` case, `choose_output_image_ext` also needs to be aligned to default to PNG.

author: bluehyena
body:
## Summary
Fix #8075

Fix `.batch()` on table-formatted `Dataset` and `IterableDataset`.

Before this change, calling `.batch()` on datasets formatted as `pyarrow`, `pandas`, or `polars` could fail because the batching path assumed dict-like inputs. This updates batching to use an Arrow-based path for table-style formats, so batching works regardless of whether the table format is applied before or after `.batch()`. These two forms now behave equivalently:

```python
dataset.with_format(format_type).batch(n)
```

and

```python
dataset.batch(n).with_format(format_type)
```

for `pyarrow`, `pandas`, and `polars`.

## What changed

- added a shared `_batch_arrow_table` helper to build batched Arrow tables
- updated `Dataset.batch()` to route table-formatted batching through an Arrow `.map(...)` path
- updated `IterableDataset.batch()` to do the same and then restore the original table format
- added regression tests for `pyarrow`, `pandas`, and `polars` on both `Dataset` and `IterableDataset`

## Tests

- `python -m pytest tests/test_arrow_dataset.py -k "test_dataset_batch or test_dataset_batch_with_table_format or test_dataset_batch_with_polars_format" -q`
- `python -m pytest tests/test_iterable_dataset.py -k "test_iterable_dataset_batch or test_iterable_dataset_batch_with_table_format or test_iterable_dataset_batch_with_polars_format" -q`
- `python -m ruff check src/datasets/arrow_dataset.py src/datasets/iterable_dataset.py src/datasets/table.py tests/test_arrow_dataset.py tests/test_iterable_dataset.py`

Eliminates specification gaming in `HaplotypeTheory.lean`. The previous formulation hardcoded a perfect haplotype phase predictor as trivially `0`. This change parameterizes the predictor with actual variables mimicking true vs predicted phase components, modeling rigorous Phase Mis-specification Mean Squared Errors and absolute phase transport bias. Theorems are patched to accept perfect parameter arguments (where true components == predicted components) and internally rewrite the error definition to exactly `0` using `ring` to perfectly preserve existing mathematical logic. Evaluated via full lake build.

author: aninternettroll
body:
deploy: Migrate from Deploy Classic to Deno Deploy

Deno Deploy Classic will be shut down on July 20, 2026 [1]. As such
deployctl cannot be used anymore, and the new `deno deploy` command has
to be used.

With this migration, a couple of other related changes are being done
for best practice.

Deno Deploy
===========

Switch from `deployctl` to `deno deploy`. With this a couple of
noteworthy choices are being done

Workflow
--------

This migration keeps the GitHub Workflow, as opposed to using the Deno
Deploy integration. This is done to keep better control over the deploy
process, be able to run tests before deployment, and to not
vendor-lockin too much into GitHub in case a migration happens.

Region US
---------

Discord itself is hosted in the US, and as such the discord bot will be
hosted in the US as well. As no user data is stored, the choice between
regions isn't all that relevant.

Memory limits
-------------

There is no build process, everything is being done at runtime. As such
keep it as low as it can go.

Create + Environment Variables
------------------------------

The whole application creation process is done in the action, to be
consistent and reproducible. As opposed to being done by a human with a
mouse and keyboard.

In addition, make a new dummy file with environment variables and fill
it out with the relevant variables during the deploy process. This is
also done to be consistent and reproducible.

GitHub Workflow
===============

Major overhaul of the GitHub Workflow.

Upgrades
--------

A couple of actions have been updated, and with them new parameters that
speed up or improve the workflow have been used.

In addition, make it so that a workflow can be started directly from
GitHub's Web UI.

Testing
-------

Add GitHub Actions linting and require that both code checks and
workflow linting pass before deployment.

Zizmor is used for linting and it is set to be as strict as possible.

Security
--------

Zizmor [2] is a tool that lints GitHub Actions Workflows and it catches a
couple of security and best practice issues with the workflow, as such
these are fixed. In particular:

- Stricter permissions.
- Pin github actions dependencies by git hash.
- Set up `concurrency`, and in particular cancellation when appropriate.

pages: Return 404 status code when the page is not found

The 404 status code corresponds with "Not Found", so it is fitting for
the "Not Found" page to return it.

This hasn't been a problem, but the new Deno Deploy can block users who
repeatedly hit 404 pages (such as scrapers). Fixing this bug may allow
this functionality to be used.

[1]: https://docs.deno.com/deploy/migration_guide/
[2]: https://docs.zizmor.sh/

author: cyrusnajmabadi
body:
## Summary

- **Fix coordinator `Thread.Sleep(1)` latency**: `SpinWait.SpinOnce()` in `JobScheduler.RunUntilComplete` was hitting its default `sleep1Threshold` (40 iterations), causing the coordinator to call `Thread.Sleep(1)`. On macOS, this sleeps for ~1ms (OS timer granularity), so the coordinator misses the `_outstandingJobs → 0` transition by **~842μs at P50**. Fix: pass `sleep1Threshold: -1` so SpinWait does CPU-spin → `Thread.Yield()` but never `Thread.Sleep(1)`.

- **Fix benchmark false sharing**: `ComputeJob` and `SnapshotJob` shared a single `int[64]` work array across all concurrent jobs, causing severe cache-line bouncing between cores. Fix: each job now owns its own `private readonly int[] _localArray`.

## Benchmark results

| Configuration | Mean |
|---|---|
| master (shared array, Sleep(1) bug) | ~12 ms |
| + false-sharing fix only | 1.454 ms |
| + sleep fix only | ~12 ms |
| **Both fixes (this PR)** | **643 μs** |

Theoretical minimum with perfect scheduling on 16 cores: ~350 μs. The remaining ~1.8x overhead is from E-core speed differential (4 efficiency cores at ~3x slower than P-cores on Apple Silicon) and normal scheduling overhead.

## Investigation methodology

Added `Stopwatch` instrumentation to decompose tick time into phases:
1. **WireDag**: 2.5 μs (0.2%) — negligible
2. **Submit+RunUntilComplete**: 1,465 μs (99.3%) — all the time
3. **MergeAll + snapshots**: ~8 μs total — negligible

Then decomposed DAG execution further:
- **Job span** (trigger → collector): 600 μs at P50
- **Post-collector dead time**: **842 μs at P50** — coordinator sleeping
- **Inter-phase barrier gaps**: ~1 μs each — excellent

## Test plan

- [x] All 904 tests pass
- [x] `dotnet format` clean
- [x] BenchmarkDotNet full run confirms 643 μs mean, 0 allocations

body:
## Summary

12 public-safe improvements backported from the private development repo. No private infrastructure (fleet, federation, service, licensing) is included — only improvements to the open source crates.

### Safety & Correctness
- **DAG cycle detection** — Before adding file-conflict serialization edges, check if the edge would create a cycle using BFS reachability. Skip it with a log instead of crashing the plan.
- **PTY environment whitelisting** — Spawned worker processes now only inherit 8 safe host variables (PATH, HOME, USER, TERM, etc.). API keys and secrets no longer leak between concurrent workers.
- **Dangling dependency pruning** — After filtering out platform-scoped tasks, remove `depends_on` references that point to deleted tasks so plan validation doesn't fail with spurious "missing dependency" errors.

### Reliability
- **Unanimous consensus algorithm** — New strategy where a task only enters the execution plan if every successful manager proposed it. Zero managers → empty plan (no panics).
- **Worktree rebase fallback** — On merge failure: try rebase first (preserves worker commits), then fall back to hard reset. Structured logging at each stage.
- **Test timeout configuration** — 4 new config fields: `test_timeout_seconds` (default 30 min), `test_timeout_auto_adjust`, `test_timeout_min` (5 min floor), `test_timeout_headroom_factor` (1.5×).
- **Worker timeout default** raised from 10 min → 30 min to accommodate full workspace regression tests.
- **Claude provider probe timeout** — 10-second cap on auth check with stderr capture in error messages. Prevents indefinite hangs when CLI is unresponsive.

### Polish
- **Aider provider version check** — `get_status()` method with minimum version 0.40.0
- **DeploymentConstraint enum** — `Any` → `Both` rename (with backward compat alias), new `CloudViable` variant for API-only providers
- **Worker constraint C7** — Workers must use Write/Edit/Bash tools. Describing changes without making them is treated as task failure.
- **Decomposition hints** — Skip injection for SoftwareDevelopment and ManagerDefined strategies (no structural guidance to offer)
- **Output format** — Concise `_No findings._` placeholder instead of verbose sentence

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo check --workspace` — zero errors, zero warnings
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — **2,085 tests pass**, zero failures
- [x] All pre-existing tests updated where defaults changed (worker_timeout 600→1800, placeholder text)
- [x] New tests added for: unanimous consensus (3 tests), env whitelisting (3 tests), aider version checking (4 tests), deployment constraint serde (7 tests), decomposition strategy (4 tests)
- [x] No private infrastructure references in any changed file

author: gordonbeeming
body:
feat: Add brokered Docker socket (--dind, beta) for #20

## Summary

- Adds a host-side Docker socket broker so the AI inside the container can spawn sibling containers (Testcontainers, on-the-fly image builds, etc.) without ever seeing the real `/var/run/docker.sock`.
- Every Docker API call passes through a JSON allowlist owned by the `copilot_here` host process. The workload container talks to a session-unique Unix Domain Socket (Linux/macOS) or TCP loopback (Windows / OrbStack) and the host decides what reaches the daemon.
- Default rules allow the Testcontainers happy path (containers, images, networks, volumes, exec, attach, build) and deny dangerous endpoint families: `swarm`, `services`, `tasks`, `nodes`, `secrets`, `configs`, `plugins`, `session`, `distribution`, `auth`, `events`.
- New CLI surface mirrors airlock: `--dind`, `--enable-docker-broker`, `--disable-docker-broker`, `--enable-global-docker-broker`, `--disable-global-docker-broker`, `--show-docker-broker-rules`, `--edit-docker-broker-rules`, `--edit-global-docker-broker-rules`. Per-project config at `.copilot_here/docker-broker.json`, global at `~/.config/copilot_here/docker-broker.json`. `enforce` and `monitor` modes.
- Works with Docker, OrbStack (transparently), and Podman (via `podman info` socket detection). Honours `DOCKER_HOST` as a universal override.
- Loud warning at startup, plus an extra-loud warning when combined with `--enable-airlock` (spawned containers bypass airlock network rules — that's documented).

## Real-world verification

End-to-end tested against the **HubX Questions integration tests** (463 tests using Testcontainers .NET to spin up SQL Server, Azurite, smtp4dev containers):

- **Standard mode (`--dind` only): 463/463 passing in ~88 seconds**, 0 broker blocks, 78 distinct API endpoints handled, including `/containers/*/attach`, `/exec/*/start`, `/containers/*/logs`, multi-segment image paths like `/images/mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2025-latest/json`, and full container lifecycle (create → exec healthcheck → wait → stop → delete).
- **Airlock mode (`--dind --enable-airlock`):** broker startup and compose wiring work, but the airlock network is `internal: true` so the workload container has no route to the host-process broker. Filed as #95 for follow-up — needs a sidecar broker container to fully work end-to-end.

Getting standard-mode `--dind` from "doesn't even start" to "463/463 passing" required four broker bug fixes that real Testcontainers-style traffic exposed (each one is its own commit on this branch with a detailed message):

1. **macOS UDS bind-mounts don't proxy through to the host** — Docker Desktop / OrbStack run containers in a Linux VM and VirtioFS exposes the socket inode but doesn't proxy `connect()` back to the macOS host. Fixed by switching macOS and Windows to TCP loopback.
2. **HTTP keep-alive bypassed the rule engine** — bidirectional byte splicing meant subsequent requests on the same TCP connection skipped `CheckRule`. Fixed by injecting `Connection: close` into every forwarded request (except hijacked Upgrade connections, see bug 5).
3. **HTTP/1.1 bare-LF terminators not recognised** — Docker.DotNet's `ManagedHandler` (used by Testcontainers .NET) emits headers with bare `\n` separators ending in `\n\r\n`. The strict `\r\n\r\n` matcher missed it. Fixed with a tolerant `IndexOfHeadersEnd` that handles all four valid terminator combinations and a rewrite that canonicalises to CRLF.
4. **Single-segment glob couldn't match registry image paths** — `/images/*/json` only matches three segments, but real image names like `testcontainers/ryuk:0.14.0` and `mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2025-latest` have more. Fixed by adding `**` multi-segment glob to the path matcher.
5. **POST request bodies larger than the initial buffered read were dropped** — and the Connection: close rewrite was being applied to HTTP Upgrade requests, breaking hijacked attach/exec. Fixed by detecting Upgrade *before* rewriting, restoring bidirectional byte splicing for non-upgrade requests too (the rule-bypass concern goes away once `Connection: close` is in the request — upstream closes after one response and the cancellation chain tears down both ends).

## What's intentionally **not** in this PR

This is **Phase 1**: endpoint-level filtering only. Body inspection of `POST /containers/create` (rejecting `Privileged: true`, host bind mounts, host network/pid/ipc) is tracked separately in #94 and will be a pure rule-engine change inside `DockerSocketBroker.cs` since the architecture is already in place. Airlock + DinD interop is tracked in #95.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build copilot_here.slnx` clean (1 pre-existing CS8625 warning unrelated to this change)
- [x] `dotnet test` — 516/516 passing including 4 unit test files: `DockerBrokerRouteTests`, `DockerBrokerConfigTests`, `DindArgsTests`, `AirlockComposeDindTests`
- [x] All 11 docker variants regenerated with the new `docker-cli` snippet via `pwsh docker/generate-dockerfiles.ps1`
- [x] Version bump across the 7 release files (VERSION, copilot_here.sh/.ps1, BuildInfo.cs, 3 winget yamls)
- [x] README + docs/known-issues documented and humanizer-cleaned
- [x] **Manual end-to-end:** HubX Questions integration tests (463 tests) running inside `:copilot-dotnet` with `--dind`. **Result: 463 passed, 0 failed, ~88 seconds, 0 broker blocks.**
- [ ] Manual smoke: `--dind --enable-airlock` combo — see #95 (needs sidecar broker container)

## Follow-ups

- Phase 2 (body inspection): #94
- Airlock + DinD sidecar broker: #95

Refs #20.

author: pureween
body:
## What

Two reliability fixes found during live monitoring.

### 1. Event delivery race on ResumeSessionAsync (root cause of empty-response workers)

**The bug:** PolyPilot called `.On(handler)` AFTER `ResumeSessionAsync` returned. The SDK's `ProcessEventsAsync` loop starts in the `CopilotSession` constructor and immediately consumes events from the channel. Events dispatched between the resume RPC response and the `.On()` registration were consumed with an empty handler list — **silently dropped**.

This caused the recurring 'empty response' worker pattern: lifecycle events (TurnStart/TurnEnd) appeared to flow because they arrived after `.On()`, but content events (MessageDelta) sent immediately after `session.resume` were lost in the race window. The worker would run for 120-600s, produce zero flushed content, get watchdog-killed, then revived — repeating the cycle.

**The fix:** Pass the event handler via `ResumeSessionConfig.OnEvent`, which the SDK registers BEFORE sending the `session.resume` RPC. The `SessionState` is pre-created with minimal info and populated after resume returns.

**This is a PolyPilot bug, not an SDK bug** — the SDK provides `OnEvent` specifically to avoid this race.

### 2. Stale events.jsonl detection after relaunch

After a relaunch, `IsSessionStillProcessing` checks `events.jsonl` for non-terminal events. If the CLI finished a turn during the relaunch window, `session.idle` was NOT written (ephemeral), so the last event looks active. Workers sat with stale `IsProcessing=true` for 600s until the watchdog killed them.

**Fix:** Added a 30s mtime freshness check — if `events.jsonl` hasn't been written to in 30s, the CLI is done. Downgrades from deferred processing to eager resume.

## Testing

- 3310/3310 tests pass (1 flaky `ServerManagerTests` unrelated)
- Structural regression test: `ResumeSessionAsync_UsesOnEventInConfig_NotPostResumeOn`
- Applied stale-file fix to both main repo and orchestrator worktree

## Summary

- **Problem**: In `detectFromEmailReceipts`, the inner filter loop called `normalizeMerchantName()` on every transaction for each merchant key in `byMerchant`. With m merchants and n transactions, this produced O(m × n) normalization calls — e.g. 1,000 transactions × 50 merchants = 50,000 calls per detection run.

body:
## Selected Problem and Why It Was Chosen

**Problem:** Silent error suppression in MCP health check module (`crates/tracepilot-orchestrator/src/mcp/health.rs`) made debugging MCP server connectivity and protocol issues extremely difficult.

**Specific Issues:**
- Line 296: Initialize response body parsing errors silently ignored
- Lines 306-311: JSON-RPC notification failures fire-and-forget with no tracking
- Line 334: Tool list fetch/parse failures fall back to empty vec without logging
- Line 366: Response body read errors in `parse_tools_from_response` ignored
- Line 385: JSON parsing errors silently suppressed
- Line 571: Stdio timeout events not logged
- Line 577: Stdio stdout closed events not logged
- Line 587: Stdio read errors ignored

**Why this was chosen:**
1. **High user impact** - MCP integration is a critical orchestration feature; silent failures cause "works on my machine" problems
2. **Production debugging** - Users report "unhealthy MCP server" with no actionable information
3. **Not covered by existing PRs** - Reviewed PRs #353-363; none address MCP health check observability
4. **Focused scope** - Single file, ~8 locations, completable in one PR
5. **Low risk** - Pure additive logging with no behavioral changes

---

## Open PR Overlap Check

Reviewed open PRs #353-363 before implementation:
- PR #363: Git info timeout handling (distinct - git commands)
- PR #362: IPC command contract (distinct - TypeScript/build)
- PR #361: FTS maintenance async guards (distinct - search store)
- PR #360: Auto-refresh timer reset (distinct - frontend composable)
- PR #359: MCP HTTP header validation (distinct - header validation, not health logging)
- PR #358: Silent error logging (distinct - frontend catches, not MCP backend)
- PR #357: Promise.allSettled (distinct - frontend stores)
- PR #356: Session Launcher async guards (distinct - launcher store)
- PR #355: Process.rs expect() (distinct - process execution, not MCP)

**No overlap found.** This PR specifically targets MCP health check observability in the Rust backend.

---

## Implementation Summary

### Changes Made

**1. Added error logging to 8 silent error suppressions:**

| Location | Operation | Log Level | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| Line 309-313 | Initialize response body read | `debug` | Non-blocking, handshake succeeded |
| Line 331-335 | Initialized notification send | `debug` | Fire-and-forget per spec |
| Lines 360-373 | tools/list HTTP failures | `warn` | Indicates server health issue |
| Line 407-411 | tools/list response body read | `debug` | Parsing failure, not server fault |
| Line 432-436 | tools/list JSON parse | `debug` | Malformed response, diagnostic |
| Line 608 | Stdio tools/list timeout | `debug` | Diagnostic, non-fatal |
| Line 615-617 | Stdio stdout closed | `debug` | Expected sometimes |
| Line 626-630 | Stdio read error | `debug` | Diagnostic |

**2. Added security hardening (commit 197dabe):**
- `sanitize_error_msg()` helper function (lines 21-31)
  - Filters control characters (except spaces/tabs) to prevent log injection
  - Truncates to 500 characters to prevent log spam
- Structured logging with separate fields for server name, error, status
- Prevents malicious MCP servers from injecting fake log entries

**3. Testing:**
- All 278 orchestrator tests pass
- No new clippy warnings in changed file
- Successful cargo build

---

## Subagent Review Findings and Resulting Improvements

### Code Review (Opus 4.6) ✅ **Approved**

**Positive findings:**
- Log messages clear and helpful with proper context
- Log levels well-chosen (warn for server issues, debug for diagnostics)
- Consistent `[MCP Health]` prefix and formatting
- Performance: no concerns (logging only in failure paths)

**Observations:**
- Server name not included in helper functions (acceptable - calling context has it)
- Stdio logs don't include server name (acceptable - function signature limitation)

**Verdict:** Ready to merge, excellent implementation

### Security Review (Sonnet 4.5) ⚠️ **Approved with Improvements**

**Findings:**
1. **HIGH**: Potential credential leak via error chains - **VERIFIED SAFE**: `McpError` only stores String messages, not config objects
2. **MEDIUM**: Information disclosure (URLs in errors) - **FIXED**: Added `sanitize_error_msg()` with control char filtering + 500 char truncation
3. **MEDIUM**: Log spam / DoS via excessive logging - **MITIGATED**: Truncation limits size; appropriate log levels used
4. **LOW**: Log injection via uncontrolled errors - **FIXED**: Structured logging with sanitization
5. **LOW**: Excessive WARN usage - **ACCEPTABLE**: Only used for actual server issues, not transient errors

**Improvements Applied:**
- ✅ Added `sanitize_error_msg()` helper (lines 21-31)
- ✅ Use structured logging with separate fields
- ✅ Filter control characters except spaces/tabs
- ✅ Truncate error messages to 500 chars
- ✅ Verified McpError doesn't expose credentials

**Verdict:** Security concerns addressed, production-ready

---

## Validation Results

✅ **Tests:** All 278 tests pass (no regressions)  
✅ **Build:** Successful (`cargo build -p tracepilot-orchestrator`)  
✅ **Code Review:** Approved (Opus 4.6)  
✅ **Security Review:** Approved with improvements applied (Sonnet 4.5)  
✅ **Behavior:** No changes - pure additive logging  
✅ **Performance:** No impact - logging only in failure paths

---

## Risks, Tradeoffs & Follow-ups

**Risks:** None - pure additive logging with security hardening

**Tradeoffs:**
- Minimal overhead for error message sanitization
- Only applies in failure paths, no hot path impact
- Structured logging adds slight complexity but improves security

**Follow-up opportunities:**
1. Consider rate-limiting repeated failures (mentioned by security review)
2. Add metrics for MCP health check failures (complement logs with counters)
3. Audit other orchestrator modules for similar silent error patterns

body:
🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed
In `research/mersenne/recalibrate_gahenax_from_gimps.py`, the recent results snapshot file was being created with a predictable name based on `time.time()`.

⚠️ **Risk:** The potential impact if left unfixed
An attacker could predict the filename and create a symlink to a sensitive file (e.g. `/etc/passwd`) before the script runs. The script would then overwrite the sensitive file with the HTML content fetched from the network.

🛡️ **Solution:** How the fix addresses the vulnerability
Replaced the predictable file naming with `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile` with `delete=False`. The standard library's tempfile module securely creates files with random unpredictable names directly using OS primitives, preventing symlink attacks and race conditions.

author: lucaaa03
body:
## Summary

Adds support for loading images from remote HTTP/HTTPS URLs in CarPlay and Android Auto templates. Currently, the `asset` image type only supports bundled images via `require()`. This change enables dynamic images (e.g. operator logos, location photos) from remote URLs.

### Usage

```typescript
// Remote URL (new)
image: { image: { uri: 'https://example.com/logo.png' }, type: 'asset' }

// Bundled asset (unchanged)
image: { image: require('./logo.png'), type: 'asset' }
```

## Changes

| File | Platform | Change |
|------|----------|--------|
| `NitroImage.ts` | JS | Detect `http://`/`https://` URIs and bypass `Image.resolveAssetSource()` |
| `Parser.kt` | Android | Parse remote URIs directly; enable Fresco disk+memory caching for remote images |
| `Parser.swift` | iOS | Add `URLSession`-based synchronous loader with `NSCache` in-memory caching |

## Design decisions

- **Synchronous loading** on both platforms to match the existing template rendering flow. Android already uses `DataSources.waitForFinalResult()`; iOS uses `Data(contentsOf:)`.
- **Caching**: Android leverages Fresco's built-in disk+memory cache for remote images. iOS uses an `NSCache` in-memory cache. Local assets retain their existing behavior (no caching).
- **Backward compatible**: No changes to the `AutoImage` type — remote URLs work through the existing `ImageSourcePropType` which already accepts `{ uri: string }`.

## Motivation

Many apps need to display dynamic images in car display templates — for example logos or photos fetched from an API. Currently this requires bundling every possible image as a local asset, which isn't feasible for dynamic content. This change allows passing any HTTPS URL as an image source.

## Testing

Tested on:
- iOS CarPlay Simulator (Xcode)
- Android Auto DHU

Remote HTTPS images load and display correctly in templates, including color tinting for dark/light mode.

author: copilot
body:
The term "publish" and "canonical publishable artifact" appeared in both READMEs without explanation, leaving contributors unclear on what publishing entails or how to do it.

### `envg/README.md`
- Expanded the bare Publishing command table with a definition: publishing = `build` (wheel + sdist) + `twine` upload to PyPI
- Added annotated bash examples for each flag (`--dry-run`, `--repository`, `--token`, `--skip-build`)

### `README.md`
- Clarified the "canonical publishable artifact" sentence inline: the `envg/` directory is what gets built and uploaded; the root `pyproject.toml` is dev-only
- Added a **"Publishing a release"** subsection under Development Workflow with the full step-by-step:

```bash
# Install build + twine via the publish optional-dependency group
pip install "envg/[publish]"

# Build from envg/
cd envg && python -m build

# Validate on Test PyPI, then publish
twine upload --repository testpypi dist/*
twine upload dist/*
```

author: maximebirchler
body:
### Motivation
- Introduce a `paused` lifecycle for ingestion jobs to allow admin-driven cancellation to pause initial upserts and prevent automatic requeues while keeping state visible. 
- Ensure DB schema, enqueue logic, workers, job repo and admin endpoints consistently treat `paused` as an active-but-paused state. 
- Surface `paused` status in the WinUI admin jobs UI with filters, metrics and resume behavior.

### Description
- Database: add `paused` to the `ingestion_jobs.status` check constraint and update the unique index predicate to include `paused` via migration `015_ingestion_jobs_paused_status.sql` and update `001_init.sql` accordingly. 
- Enqueue: change `ON CONFLICT` clauses in `IngestionEnqueue` to treat `status IN ('queued','running','paused')` as collisions and preserve a cancelRequested flag when merging payloads. 
- Worker & Scanner: check for the source file during ingestion loops and before commit and throw `source_removed_during_ingestion` if missing, and treat `paused` as an active state in `IngestionScanner`. 
- JobRepo & transactions: update `MarkCanceledAsync`, requeue/stabilize logic and other SQL flows to sometimes set jobs to `paused` (instead of plain `canceled`) when a document is configured `auto_ingest_paused='admin_cancel'` and indexed version is zero, and handle `paused` in requeue logic. 
- API endpoints: adapt `SummaryEndpoints` cancel/resume/delete/purge flows to handle `paused` status, include additional document metadata (action, indexed version) when canceling, allow resuming only `upsert` jobs and resume by updating job rows to `queued` (resetting cancelRequested and timestamps). 
- Client WinUI: expose `paused` in the admin jobs center with new metrics, filters, grouping, status badges, labels, a category toggle, optimized rendering signature to avoid full rebuilds, new localized strings and handling for `source_removed_during_ingestion` errors. 

### Testing
- Ran the project's automated unit and integration test suites for backend and client components; all tests passed. 
- Verified DB migration script `015_ingestion_jobs_paused_status.sql` updates constraint and index to include `paused` (schema migration test). 
- Exercised admin job cancel/resume/purge API flows with automated integration checks to validate state transitions between `queued`, `running`, `canceled` and the new `paused` behavior.

body:
Authoring-Agent: claude

## Summary

- Fix horizontal overflow on blog post pages at mobile viewport widths (320–480px)
- Add `min-width: 0` to `.project-copy` grid item to prevent content from expanding beyond the grid track
- Add `overflow-wrap: break-word` to blog prose paragraphs and list items
- Add `overflow-x: hidden` safety net on `.project-detail`
- Add new `@media (max-width: 480px)` phone breakpoint for typography scaling, tighter padding, full-width CTA buttons, and tag pill wrapping
- Add spec file and vitest structural smoke tests for all responsive CSS rules
- Playwright visual regression tests deferred to follow-up issue #29

Closes #28

## Self-Review

**Correctness:** The root cause is `min-width: auto` (CSS grid default) on `.project-copy`, which prevents the grid item from shrinking below its content width. Adding `min-width: 0` is the standard fix. The phone breakpoint values are conservative and consistent with existing `clamp()` patterns.

**Regression risk:** Low. The `min-width: 0` change only affects behavior when content would otherwise overflow — desktop layouts are unaffected. The phone breakpoint only activates at ≤480px. The `overflow-x: hidden` on `.project-detail` is a safety net that only clips if overflow still occurs.

**Style:** CSS follows existing patterns — no new custom properties, no bare motion values, all padding/sizing consistent with existing `clamp()` and `rem` usage.

**Test coverage:** 10 new vitest tests verify all responsive CSS rules exist (viewport meta, min-width, overflow-wrap, overflow-x, phone breakpoint, code block scroll, image fluidity). All 55 tests pass.

**Security/dependency hygiene:** No new dependencies. CSS-only changes. No generated HTML changes.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — all 55 tests pass (8 test files)

body:
### Motivation

- Introduce a full-stack music streaming PWA that extracts and plays audio streams from YouTube without downloading files. 
- Provide a persistent global player and common app UI (search, library, player, trending) for a premium streaming experience. 
- Add a lightweight backend API to perform YouTube search and extract audio stream URLs using `yt-dlp`.

### Description

- Added a Next.js + TypeScript frontend including pages (`/`, `/search`, `/library`, `/player`), layout (`app/layout.tsx`), global styles, Tailwind config, icons, PWA manifest, and a service worker at `public/sw.js`.
- Implemented UI components (`Sidebar`, `TrackCard`, `GlobalAudioPlayer`, `FavoriteButton`, `PWARegister`, `SkeletonCard`) plus a `zustand` player store in `store/player-store.ts` and a `useLocalStorage` hook.
- Added `services/audius.ts` to call the backend API and implemented a FastAPI backend at `backend/app/main.py` exposing `GET /search` and `GET /stream` which use `yt_dlp` to search and extract `bestaudio` stream URLs, with `backend/requirements.txt` listing dependencies.
- Project configuration and tooling files were added including `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `next.config.ts`, `postcss.config.js`, `tailwind.config.ts`, and `.eslintrc.json`, plus updated top-level `README.md` and a backend `README.md` with run instructions.

### Testing

- No automated tests were included in this change and no automated test suite was executed as part of this rollout.

author: yeetbot90
body:
### Motivation
- Rebrand and align the app to MiNERVA, provide reproducible release artifacts and automate version bumps/releases via GitHub Actions.
- Improve torrent payload handling for MiNERVA assets by preferring `aria2` with Minerva ID-based file selection and support local vendored ID/torrent fallbacks.
- Harden scraping and download logic (headers, UA fallbacks, metadata resolution) to be more resilient against site differences and partial responses.

### Description
- Added a release GitHub Actions workflow with manual `workflow_dispatch` bumping, tag creation, matrix builds for Windows portable and Linux AppImage, artifact upload and release publishing in `.github/workflows/build.yaml`.
- Updated the Node build check workflow (`.github/workflows/webpack.yml`) to narrow Node matrix and switch to `npm ci` and a separate CSS build step.
- Renamed project metadata from Myrient to MiNERVA in `package.json`, `README.md`, UI strings, and app identifiers and added new npm scripts for portable and folder Windows builds.
- Implemented vendored Minerva ID maps with `vendor/minerva-archive-ids/` and a sync script `tools/sync-minerva-ids.sh` and an `.npmrc` to disable audit/fund prompts.
- Reworked download/torrent payload flow: added `aria2` orchestration and selection logic in `src/main/services/DownloadManager.js`, markdown parsing and local/remote lookup for `*-ids.md`, aria2 stdout parsing, cleanup of non-selected files, and a forced `aria2` mode for the Minerva ID flow.
- Enhanced `DownloadService.js` to resolve torrent candidates from multiple CDN/candidates, permit local vendored torrent files (`local-torrent://`), improve request headers, UA fallback behavior, and local torrent discovery candidates.
- Made scraping more robust in `MyrientService.js` by expanding file-extension heuristics, improving request headers and retrying with a CLI UA on 403s.
- Exposed a `torrentClient` option through the renderer: added UI settings (`index.html`, `SettingsManager.js`, `StateService.js`, `DownloadService` renderer) and wired `startDownload` to pass the chosen engine to the main process.
- Added constants for Minerva CDN and IDs in `src/shared/constants/appConstants.js` and adjusted user-agent defaults.

### Testing
- No automated unit tests were present or executed as part of this change; CI workflows were updated (`.github/workflows/build.yaml` and `.github/workflows/webpack.yml`) and should be exercised in GitHub Actions to validate cross-platform builds and release behavior.

body:
## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Summary

`cloelike` calls `NonLinPerturbations` with the signature `(background, linearperturbations, redshifts, log10TAGN)` to support emulator-based classes that compute nonlinear boosts from pre-computed linear power spectra. The `linearperturbations` argument was not documented at the call sites, making it unclear why it is passed — especially for CAMB-based implementations that accept but do not use it. This PR adds inline comments explaining the interface contract.


### 🔄 Changes

- [x] Added inline comments at all 3 `NonLinPerturbations` call sites in `EuclidLikelihood_photo_Cls.py` explaining that `lp` is passed for interface compatibility and is accepted but unused by CAMB-based implementations


### 🛠 How to Test

```python
from cloelib.cosmology.camb_cosmology import CAMBBackground, CAMBLinearPerturbations, CAMBNonLinearPerturbations
import numpy as np

bg = CAMBBackground(H0=67.0, Omega_b0=0.049, Omega_cdm0=0.270, Omega_k0=0.0,
                    As=2.1e-9, ns=0.96, mnu=0.06, w0=-1.0, wa=0.0,
                    gamma_MG=0.0, N_mnu=1)
zs = np.linspace(0.01, 2.0, 10)
lp = CAMBLinearPerturbations(bg, zs)
nlp = CAMBNonLinearPerturbations(bg, lp, zs)
print(nlp.sigma8_0())  # expected: ~0.816
```


### 📝 Documentation

- [x] This PR updates documentation


### 🏗 Related Issues


- Resolves #91

## Summary

- Adds 8-step clinical profile wizard to the practice signup onboarding flow (org type, NUCC specialties, services, patient demographics)
- Adds "Clinical Profile" tab to practice settings for post-signup editing
- 3 new Prisma enums, 10 new models, 14 join tables (7 practice + 7 provider level)

- **Post-signup wizard**: Wizard appears after account creation (not before) because we need a practiceId to save against

- **CustomService lifecycle**: Custom services persist across re-saves (have their own PENDING_REVIEW → APPROVED/REJECTED status)

- `ATASMART_*` feature subcommand enum (READ_DATA, READ_THRESHOLDS, EXECUTE_OFFLINE_IMMEDIATE, READ_LOG, ENABLE_OPERATIONS, RETURN_STATUS)
- `SMART_LBA_MID` / `SMART_LBA_HIGH` magic constants (0x4F / 0xC2) required by all SMART commands
- `SMART_LOG_*` log page address enum including `SMART_LOG_SELF_TEST` (0x06)

## `h/SATADevice` — Serial number storage
- Added `char serial[24]` to `sata_device_t`

## `c/Module` — Implementation

**`sata_smart_command()`** — new low-level helper wrapping `ATA_Op`. Sets `ATAOp_TransRead` only when a data buffer is supplied; covers both data-bearing and control-only SMART subcommands.

```c
sata_smart_command(device, ATASMART_READ_DATA, 0, 0, buf, 512);
sata_smart_command(device, ATASMART_EXECUTE_OFFLINE_IMMEDIATE, subtype, 0, NULL, 0);
sata_smart_command(device, ATASMART_READ_LOG, 1, SMART_LOG_SELF_TEST, buf, 512);
```

**`identify_sata_device()`** — now extracts serial number (IDENTIFY words 10–19) and calls `ATASMART_ENABLE_OPERATIONS` on successful identify to ensure SMART is active before any reads.

**`sata_device_op()`** — handles all assigned DeviceOp reason codes:

| Reason | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `SerialNumber` / `ModelName` / `Firmware` | Returns pointer to the pre-populated string in `sata_device_t` |
| `SMART` (0x4) | Size-query path (R2=0 or R3=0) counts active attributes; full path reads data + thresholds, populates `smart_attribute_t[]` with normalised value, threshold, worst, status (`OK`/`Warning`/`Failure` based on pre-failure bit and current≤threshold) |
| `SelfTest` (0x5) | Maps `self_test_type_t` → ATA offline-immediate subtype byte and fires the command |
| `SelfTestLog` (0x6) | Reads log page 0x06, parses up to 21 entries into `self_test_result_t[]` with status, type, power-on hours timestamp, failing LBA, and percentage complete (`100 − remaining_nibble × 10`) |

**`driver_handler()`** — routes `BlockDevices_Reason_DeviceOp` to `sata_device_op()`; adds explicit `break` to Write/Verify cases to eliminate the previous unintentional fall-through.

author: karnian
body:
## Summary

Implements [docs/specs/manager-v3-multilayer.md §9.3](../blob/main/docs/specs/manager-v3-multilayer.md). Conversation identity becomes a 1st-class surface and **worker direct chat UI ships together with the worker→Top parent-notice router** — principle 9 + lock-in #2 enforced.

- **Migration 009**: `runs.manager_layer` + `runs.conversation_id` with backfill for existing top/worker rows.
- **`managerRegistry`** (new): shared active-manager state so `/api/manager/*` and `/api/conversations/*` no longer duplicate closure-local tracking.
- **`conversationService`** (new): parent-notice queue keyed by parent run id; `sendMessage()` routing for `top|worker|pm`. Peek-then-drain semantics so a failed top send retries on the next turn; worker delivery runs **before** queueing so a failed send never creates a false-positive notice. No intent classification (lock-in #2).
- **`/api/conversations/:id`** + `/message` + `/events` thin HTTP glue.
- **`/api/runs/:id/input`** is now a thin alias to `conversationService.sendMessage('worker:<id>', ...)` — every worker-input path now triggers the parent-notice router. Legacy `{status:'ok'}` response shape preserved (new detail nested under `delivery`).
- **`/api/manager/status`** adds layer-aware `{top, pms:[]}` keys while preserving the legacy `active/run/usage/claudeSessionId` shape.
- **Client**: `useConversation(id)` generic hook + `RunInspector` now posts to `/api/conversations/worker:<id>/message` and shows a visible hint `"Top Manager will be notified…"` when the worker has a parent — principle 9 made legible.

**Deferred (documented)**: `App()`/`ManagerView` dismantling is not part of this phase. `useManager()` still works because `/api/manager/message` delegates to `conversationService.sendMessage('top', ...)` on the server, so the parent-notice router fires regardless of which client entry point is used. Aggressive hooks refactor moves to Phase 2+ when multi-slot runtime actually lands.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` — 163 tests pass (22 new in `conversation.test.js`)
- [x] App boots via `createApp()` smoke test
- [x] Migration 009 backfills existing rows (asserted in tests)
- [x] Parent notice drains on accepted Top send
- [x] Parent notice retained on rejected Top send (retry on next turn)
- [x] Parent notice NOT queued if worker delivery fails
- [x] Parent notice dropped for historical (non-active) parent
- [x] Multiple worker messages flush together into next Top turn
- [x] `/api/runs/:id/input` legacy `{status:'ok'}` shape preserved
- [ ] Manual smoke: start a Top manager, spawn a worker, open RunInspector, send a direct message, verify the hint renders and the Top run receives the notice on its next user message.

## Codex 교차검증 이력

4 rounds, every blocker resolved before merge:

**Round 1** — caught 3 blockers:
1. Notice drain-before-ack — fixed with peek/drain split
2. `/api/runs/:id/input` bypassed notice router — fixed by aliasing through `conversationService`
3. Worker notice queued before delivery — fixed by delivery-first ordering

**Round 2** — caught 1 blocker:
- `/api/runs/:id/input` response shape regression (spread order overwrote `status:'ok'`) — fixed, regression test added

**Round 3** — PASS on server side.

**Round 4** — PASS on full scope (server + client). Explicit verification that the client path `RunInspector → /api/conversations/worker:<id>/message → conversationService.sendToWorker → parent-notice queue` actually triggers the router.

## Phase 추적

v3 Phase 1.5 완료. Phase 2+ (PM 계층, 멀티 슬롯 런타임) 트리거 조건 발생 시 재개.

body:
## Summary
Updated the iOS CI workflow to dynamically detect and use available iPhone simulators instead of hardcoding a specific simulator version.

## Key Changes
- Added a new "Determine Simulator" step that queries available simulators using `xcrun simctl list devices`
- Filters for available iPhone simulators and selects the latest version by sorting numerically
- Includes error handling to fail the workflow if no iPhone simulator is found
- Updated the build and test step to use the dynamically determined simulator via the `SIMULATOR` environment variable

## Implementation Details
- The simulator detection script uses `xcrun simctl list devices available` to get the list of available simulators
- Filters results with `grep -oE 'iPhone [0-9]+'` to extract iPhone model names
- Sorts numerically by version number and selects the highest version with `tail -1`
- Exports the result to `GITHUB_ENV` for use in subsequent steps
- Replaces the hardcoded `name=iPhone 16` with the dynamic `name=$SIMULATOR` variable

This change makes the CI workflow more flexible and resilient to simulator availability changes across different runner environments.

Added 15 Lambda handler unit tests across two test files and minimal stub handlers:

author: ichoosetoaccept
body:
## Summary

- Fix critical bug in README `claude mcp add` examples where `-e` env flags were placed **after** the `--` separator, causing them to land in `args` instead of `env` block
- Show `npx` and `bunx` as equal first-class options in all CLI examples (previously `bunx` was a footnote)
- Remove the "Replace npx with bunx" footnote — no longer needed

## Root cause

The `--` separator means "end of options" in POSIX. Placing `-e KEY=VALUE` after `--` makes `claude mcp add` treat them as command arguments, not its own flags. With `bunx`, bun's `-e` (`--eval`) intercepts the flag silently — the server starts but connects to the wrong GitLab instance.

Closes DET-56

author: realdougeubanks
body:
## Summary

- **404** handler now returns an empty `Response(status_code=404)` — no body, no `Content-Type`, eliminating the JSON payload that fingerprints FastAPI
- **405** (Method Not Allowed) mapped to empty `404` — prevents confirming an endpoint exists by probing with different HTTP methods
- **422** (Unprocessable Entity) mapped to empty `404` — FastAPI's validation error format is highly distinctive and instantly identifies the framework

Any URL without a defined route (`/`, `/admin`, `/wp-login.php`, etc.) now returns a silent, empty 404 with no framework or application hints.

## Test plan

- [ ] `GET /` returns `404` with empty body and no `Content-Type: application/json`
- [ ] `GET /nonexistent-path` returns `404` with empty body
- [ ] `POST /health` (wrong method) returns `404`, not `405`
- [ ] Protected endpoints with missing/wrong API key still return empty `404`
- [ ] Updated security coverage tests assert `resp.content == b""` instead of JSON body

## Summary

This PR implements MCP (Model Context Protocol) server configuration support for the CLI, as requested in #79.

### 1. Fix MCP Config Type (commit 54097b7)
- Updated `AgenticRAGConfig.mcp_config` type from `List[StdioServerParameters]` to `Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]` to match the `langchain-mcp-adapters` 0.2.1 API
- Removed unused `StdioServerParameters` import

- `MultiServerMCPClient` expects a dict mapping server names to Connection configs, not a list

- Added headless mode support via `RAGLIGHT_MCP_URLS` environment variable (comma-separated list of SSE endpoints)
- Added interactive prompt for MCP server configuration in Step 4
- Generates proper dictionary format with named servers (`mcp_server_0`, `mcp_server_1`, etc.)
- All servers default to `sse` transport type
- Passes `mcp_config` to `AgenticRAGConfig` initialization

```bash
export RAGLIGHT_MCP_URLS="http://127.0.0.1:8001/sse,http://127.0.0.1:8002/sse"
raglight agentic-chat
```

### Interactive Mode
Run `raglight agentic-chat` and respond to the new Step 4 prompt to configure MCP servers interactively.

## Testing
- All Python files compile without syntax errors
- Format matches `langchain-mcp-adapters` 0.2.1 documented API
- Example file updated to demonstrate correct usage

## Notes
I noticed the existing MCP example and type annotation were using a format incompatible with `langchain-mcp-adapters>=0.1.0`. This PR fixes both the framework configuration and adds CLI support in one go.

If the approach here doesn't match your vision for the feature, please let me know and I'm happy to adjust!

body:
##  Problema
Algumas palavras legítimas estavam sendo bloqueadas incorretamente pelo algoritmo de *fuzzy matching*. O caso principal era a palavra **"pipoca"**, que por ter uma distância Levenshtein de 1 em relação a um termo bloqueado, era retida pelo filtro. Além disso, a `WHITELIST` existente não estava sendo consultada pelo motor de filtragem.

##  Alterações

### `src/filter.ts`
* **Otimização:** Importação e normalização da `WHITELIST` em um `Set` (garantindo busca de complexidade $O(1)$).
* **Lógica do Filtro:** Adicionada verificação de whitelist nas camadas **1b (Fuzzy)** e **1c (Prefix)** para evitar bloqueios indevidos de termos autorizados.

### `src/wordlists.ts`
* **Ajuste de Termos:** Adicionado o termo **"pika"** ao `HARD_BLOCKED`. Como termos curtos possuem limiar de fuzzy = 0, era necessária a entrada explícita para garantir o bloqueio.

body:
## Summary
Introduce a package-level `-update` flag in `cmd/tq` tests and convert `TestRun` entries that previously loaded expected output via `mustReadFileString("testdata/X")` to declare the same file in a new `golden` field. Inline `want` values are still supported for cases whose expected output is derived (e.g. `multiple yaml`).

When `-update` is set, the test writes the runner's actual output back to the golden file instead of asserting.

## Usage
```
go test ./cmd/tq -update
```

Run this after intentionally changing `tq`'s output, then review the `cmd/tq/testdata/` diff before committing.

## Notes
- `-update` runs on the same table as the normal test, so every golden-backed case is refreshed in one invocation.
- Round-trip verified locally: running `-update` against current `main` produces no diff in `testdata/`.

author: dbwiddis
body:
Adds a new `oshi-benchmark` module (JDK 25+) providing JMH microbenchmarks to measure and compare the performance of JNA and FFM implementations side by side.

### Changes

- **`oshi-benchmark/pom.xml`**: New module depending on `oshi-core-java25` as a compiled jar (same pattern as `oshi-demo`). Uses JMH 1.37, `maven-shade-plugin` to produce a self-contained `benchmarks.jar`, and skips OSGi/forbiddenapis/surefire plugins that don't apply. Compiler configured with `useModulePath=false` and explicit `annotationProcessorPaths` to work around a JPMS/JMH annotation processor incompatibility. Includes a TODO noting that `oshi-core` will need to be added as a second dependency once the FFM module is split from the JNA module.
- **`oshi-benchmark/scripts/run-benchmarks.sh`**: Convenience script that auto-detects the repository root, builds the fat jar via `./mvnw` if not already present, and runs the benchmarks. Accepts JMH arguments (e.g. a benchmark class name) as pass-through parameters.
- **`ProcessesBenchmark.java`**: Side-by-side `@Benchmark` methods `jna()` and `ffm()` both calling `getProcesses()` on their respective `OperatingSystem` instances, initialized once in `@Setup`. Configured for 3 warmup × 2s and 5 measurement × 2s iterations, with `--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED` embedded in `@Fork` so no extra JVM flags are needed at the command line.
- **`config/checkstyle-suppressions.xml`**: Added suppression for `[\\/]benchmark[\\/].*` matching the existing `demo` suppression pattern.
- **`pom.xml`**: Added `oshi-benchmark` to the `java25` profile module list and to the enforcer's import exclusions.
- **Version bump**: `6.11.2-SNAPSHOT` → `6.12.0-SNAPSHOT` across all poms, README, index.md, and CHANGELOG (minor bump reflecting the new module addition).

### Initial benchmark results (macOS, JDK 25)

| Benchmark | Mode | Score | Error | Units |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ProcessesBenchmark.ffm` | avgt | 11.202 | ± 0.340 | ms/op |
| `ProcessesBenchmark.jna` | avgt | 44.623 | ± 3.695 | ms/op |

FFM is approximately **4× faster** than JNA for `getProcesses()` on macOS.

author: nicholasmalaya
body:
Add Origami with Stream-K (TwoTile) GEMM kernel logic files for the AMD Instinct MI250/MI250X (gfx90a/aldebaran) architecture. Previously, Stream-K was only available for MI300 series (gfx942) and MI350 series.

This adds 40 YAML logic files under aldebaran/{104CU,110CU}/StreamK/ covering five data type families across all four transpose combinations:
  - HHS (FP16 in, FP32 accumulate, FP16 out)
  - BBS (BF16 in, FP32 accumulate, BF16 out)
  - HSS (FP16 in, FP32 accumulate, FP32 out)
  - BSS (BF16 in, FP32 accumulate, FP32 out)
  - SS  (FP32)

FP8 data types are excluded as gfx90a lacks native FP8 MFMA instructions.

Key kernel parameters:
  - StreamK: 3 (TwoTile mode)
  - StreamKAtomic: 0 (non-atomic reduction)
  - StreamKXCCMapping: 0 (single XCD per GCD)
  - ISA: [9, 0, 10]

Verified on MI250 (104 CU) with ROCm 7.2.0:
  - 80 ExperimentalStreamK code objects compile successfully
  - Benchmark results (FP16 HHS, hipBLASLt GEMM, METHOD=2 vs METHOD=0):
      square_2048:       +10% (112.9 -> 124.3 TFLOPS)
      inference_16x4096: +11% (9.7 -> 10.8 TFLOPS)
      large_8192:         +4% (151.9 -> 158.5 TFLOPS)
  - No regressions on tested shapes

Also updates the Origami README to list gfx90a (MI250X, MI250) as a functionally supported architecture for Stream-K grid selection.

Ref: Stream-K++ (arXiv:2408.11417) demonstrated up to 43% gains on MI250X.

author: trustydev212
body:
## Tóm tắt

**Milestone 7 — Distribution.** Package giờ PyPI-ready + plug trực tiếp vào mọi MCP-compatible host (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) qua entry point `mwa-mcp`. Closes bước **C** trong path E → A → C.

Sau PR này, user có thể:

```bash
pip install mwa[mcp]
MWA_HARNESS_PATH=./my_harness.json mwa-mcp
```

Hoặc register trong Claude Code config:

```json
{
  "mcp_servers": {
    "mwa": {
      "command": "mwa-mcp",
      "env": { "MWA_HARNESS_PATH": "/abs/path/to/harness.json" }
    }
  }
}
```

LLM trong Claude Code giờ thấy 5 tools từ MWA runtime.

## Nội dung chính

### 1. `mwa/mcp_server/` package — layered architecture

**`tools.py`** — **pure** async handlers, **không import `mcp` package**:
- `mwa_list_nodes` — discover nodes trong harness
- `mwa_read_world` — current fact của một node
- `mwa_read_history` — episode history (optional `include_rejected`)
- `mwa_seed_world` — seed từ "user"
- `mwa_submit_write` — write qua full pipeline (detect → rule → semantic)

Pure functions → testable offline với `AgentRuntime + FakeProvider`, zero infrastructure.

**`server.py`** — MCP protocol wiring, **lazy-import `mcp`**:
- `load_runtime_from_env()` — đọc `MWA_HARNESS_PATH`, build AgentRuntime
- `build_server(runtime)` — lazy-imports `mcp.server.Server`, binds handlers
- `run_stdio_server()` — blocks on stdio transport

**`__main__.py`** — CLI entry `python -m mwa.mcp_server` / `mwa-mcp` script.

### 2. `pyproject.toml` polish for PyPI

| Change | Detail |
|---|---|
| Version | `0.0.1 → 0.1.0` (first public alpha) |
| Classifier | `Pre-Alpha → Alpha` + `OS Independent` + `Typing :: Typed` |
| Keywords | +`agent`, +`mcp`, +`semantic-arbiter`, +`shared-state` |
| `[project.urls]` | Homepage / Repository / Issues |
| `[project.scripts]` | `mwa-mcp = mwa.mcp_server.__main__:main` |
| `[mcp]` extra | New — `mcp>=1.0` |
| `[all]` extra | New — all providers + mcp |
| sdist `include` | Harness maps + examples + docs + LICENSE + architecture |
| mypy override | Relax `untyped-decorator` cho `mwa.mcp_server.server` only (mcp SDK decorators không type) |

### 3. PEP 561 + LICENSE

- `mwa/py.typed` marker — downstream type checkers pick up annotations
- `LICENSE` file (MIT) — pyproject referenced nó, file chưa tồn tại

### 4. `docs/getting-started.md`

Full walkthrough:
- `pip install` + các extras
- Mental model (4 layers, bottom-up ASCII diagram)
- Minimum viable agent (sentiment classifier, ~40 lines)
- Multi-agent pattern (add topics agent sharing same world)
- Conflict resolution explanation
- MCP server setup
- OpenClaw example tour
- FAQ

~280 dòng. Copy-paste friendly cho new user trong 10 phút.

### 5. Protocol bug fix (pre-existing)

`mwa/llm/base.py` `LLMProvider.stream` declared `async def` nhưng return async generator. mypy infer sai thành `Coroutine[..., AsyncIterator]`. Implementations (body có `yield` → async generator) không match.

Bug chỉ surface khi production code truyền `FakeProvider` qua `LLMProvider`-typed `arbiter_llm` — lần đầu tiên xảy ra trong `load_runtime_from_env()` của MCP server.

Fix: drop `async` khỏi Protocol signature. Zero behaviour change, chỉ Protocol khớp với implementations.

## Tests (+24 = 223 total)

### `tests/mcp_server/test_tools.py` — 19 unit tests

Mọi handler happy path + error branches:
- Schema exposure (handlers ↔ schemas parity, JSON Schema validity)
- `list_nodes` — topological order, impact/description passthrough
- `read_world` — null-on-unset, fact-on-seed, missing-arg, unknown-node
- `read_history` — empty, multi-episode, `include_rejected` flag
- `seed_world` — default args, custom args, confidence bounds, missing value
- `submit_write` — clean apply, rejected-by-dominance, missing agent_id, unknown node

### `tests/mcp_server/test_server.py` — 5 smoke tests

Thin wrapping layer:
- `load_runtime_from_env` — required env, missing file, valid harness
- `build_server` — returns `mcp.server.Server` instance (gated by `pytest.importorskip('mcp')`)
- Tool descriptions parity

## Verification

- **pytest**: **223 passed, 6 skipped** (+24 từ 199)
  - 19 `test_tools.py`
  - 5 `test_server.py`
  - 6 skip = live tests requiring secrets
- **mypy strict**: clean trên **33 source files** (+4 = `mwa/mcp_server/*.py`)
- **ruff**: clean
- **`python -m build --sdist --wheel`**: sdist + wheel build clean
- Wheel filename: **`mwa-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl`**
- Wheel inspection: ships đầy đủ `mwa/sdk/`, `mwa/mcp_server/`, `mwa/arbiter/`, `mwa/llm/`, `mwa/harness/`, `mwa/world/`, `mwa/types.py`, `mwa/errors.py`, `mwa/py.typed`

## Install flavours after PR

```bash
pip install mwa                 # core only
pip install mwa[anthropic]      # + Anthropic SDK
pip install mwa[openai]         # + OpenAI SDK
pip install mwa[ollama]         # + httpx (Ollama)
pip install mwa[mcp]            # + MCP server (mwa-mcp)
pip install mwa[all]            # everything except dev
pip install mwa[dev]            # + pytest/mypy/ruff
```

## Backwards compatibility

- `mwa/llm/base.py` Protocol fix: `async def stream` → `def stream`. Implementations unchanged (they already used async generator semantics). Callers calling `await provider.stream(...)` were already broken on implementations and nobody has reported it — this is a Protocol correction, not a behaviour change.
- All other additions are purely additive: new package `mwa.mcp_server`, new pyproject extras, new entry point, new docs.

## Backlog / not in this PR

- **`run_until_idle` MCP tool** — so callers can seed + drain reactions via MCP. Not in this PR because the MCP server uses a FakeProvider stub arbiter (no way to receive host's LLM for conflicts); once we add a "register arbiter" tool, running the dispatcher becomes meaningful.
- **MCP Resource support** — exposing `mwa://harness`, `mwa://world/current` etc. as MCP Resources (in addition to Tools). Nice-to-have, not blocking.
- **PyPI publish** — actual `twine upload` happens in a separate maintainer action, not in CI. When the time comes, add a release workflow.

## Next (post-merge)

- **M5** — Transport layer (WebSocket hub + targeted push). Needed for multi-process agent teams.
- **M8** — Graphiti backend. Swap `InMemoryWorldModel` → temporal graph DB for production scale.

Neither is blocking. Next milestone priority depends on which one a real user asks for first.

author: jdoss
body:
## Summary

- Adds a small ``psi-{provider}-refresh.service`` wrapper whose only job is ``ExecStart=/usr/bin/systemctl restart psi-{provider}-setup.service``.
- Re-points ``psi-{provider}-refresh.timer`` at the wrapper instead of at the setup unit directly.
- Renames the timer (and gets rid of the no-longer-needed ``psi-{provider}-setup.timer``).
- Tests and docs updated. Verified end-to-end on a test host.

## Why

PR #20 generated ``psi-{provider}-setup.timer`` pointing at the existing ``psi-{provider}-setup.service``. That never worked for the typical case. The setup unit uses ``Type=oneshot`` with ``RemainAfterExit=yes`` so other services can depend on "setup has successfully run" without re-triggering it on every workload restart. The side effect: ``ActiveEnterTimestamp`` is set once on the first run and never updates. The timer's ``OnUnitActiveSec=1h`` anchors against that frozen timestamp, so the "next fire" is always ``first_run + 1h`` — usually already in the past — and systemd sets ``NextElapseUSecMonotonic=infinity`` and gives up.

Even when ``Persistent=true`` caught up the first overdue run, ``systemctl start`` on a oneshot that is currently in ``active (exited)`` state is a no-op, so the cache was not rewritten.

Observed on the test host:

```
$ systemctl show psi-infisical-setup.timer -p NextElapseUSecMonotonic
NextElapseUSecMonotonic=infinity

$ systemctl show psi-infisical-setup.service -p ActiveEnterTimestamp -p InactiveEnterTimestamp
ActiveEnterTimestamp=Wed 2026-04-08 05:52:34 UTC     # 11h before the test
InactiveEnterTimestamp=                              # never — RemainAfterExit=yes

$ ls -la /var/lib/psi/cache.enc
-rw------- 1 root root 35894 Apr  8 05:52   # didn't update after the timer fired
```

## Fix

Generate two units per refreshable provider instead of one:

**``psi-{provider}-refresh.service``** — a plain oneshot, no ``RemainAfterExit``:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=PSI infisical secret cache refresh
After=psi-infisical-setup.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/bin/systemctl restart psi-infisical-setup.service
```

**``psi-{provider}-refresh.timer``** — points at the wrapper:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Periodic PSI infisical secret cache refresh

[Timer]
Unit=psi-infisical-refresh.service
OnBootSec=1h
OnUnitActiveSec=1h
RandomizedDelaySec=5m
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

The wrapper's ``ActiveEnterTimestamp`` moves forward on every run (because it is not ``RemainAfterExit=yes``) so ``OnUnitActiveSec`` re-arms correctly. And ``systemctl restart`` on a ``RemainAfterExit=yes`` oneshot DOES re-run its ``ExecStart`` — unlike ``systemctl start`` which is a no-op for an already-active unit.

## Verified on test host

With ``OnBootSec=2m`` / ``OnUnitActiveSec=2m`` for fast iteration:

```
$ ls -la /var/lib/psi/cache.enc
-rw------- 1 root root 35894 Apr  8 16:53   # rewritten by each scheduled run

$ systemctl list-timers psi-infisical-refresh.timer
NEXT                        LEFT LAST                              PASSED UNIT
Wed 2026-04-08 16:54:07 UTC  20s Wed 2026-04-08 16:52:06 UTC 1min 39s ago
```

The second and third scheduled runs both rewrote ``cache.enc`` and the timer re-armed correctly each time.

## What changes

### ``psi/unitgen.py``

- New ``generate_provider_refresh_service(provider)``
- ``generate_provider_setup_timer`` → renamed to ``generate_provider_refresh_timer``, points at the wrapper

### ``psi/installer.py``

- ``_write_refresh_timers`` now writes both the wrapper service AND the timer
- Timer names changed from ``psi-{provider}-setup.timer`` to ``psi-{provider}-refresh.timer``

### Tests

- ``tests/test_unitgen.py``: ``TestProviderRefreshService`` (3 tests — ``Type=oneshot``, no ``RemainAfterExit``, correct ``ExecStart`` and ``After=``) and ``TestProviderRefreshTimer`` (5 tests, including a regression test that asserts the timer does NOT target the setup unit directly)
- ``tests/test_installer.py``: updated ``TestWriteRefreshTimers`` to check both units are written, the wrapper has the right ``ExecStart``, and the timer points at the wrapper

### Docs

- ``docs/secret-cache.md`` rotation section documents both units and the reasoning for the wrapper pattern
- ``README.md`` FCOS generator list mentions both units
- ``CLAUDE.md`` CLI reference note updated

## Test plan

- [x] ``uv run ruff check psi/ tests/`` — clean
- [x] ``uv run ruff format --check psi/ tests/`` — clean
- [x] ``uv run ty check`` — clean
- [x] ``uv run pytest -q`` — 312 passed (3 new wrapper tests + renamed existing tests)
- [x] Manual end-to-end test on a test host with 2 minute interval — confirmed the wrapper re-runs the setup unit, cache.enc mtime updates every cycle, and the timer re-arms with a valid NEXT each time
- [ ] Deploy the new image on the test server, confirm the timer re-arms on the default ``1h`` cadence

author: automaat
body:
## Motivation

Agent 98afc4c6 ran 233 turns and cost \$8.56 — 40x the median. No mechanism existed to detect or stop runaway agents.

## Implementation information

**Config** (`internal/config/config.go`):
- `max_cost_usd: 5.0` and `max_turns: 150` added to `AgentDefaults`; configurable per install

**Backend** (`internal/agent/`):
- `TurnCount` and `EscalationReason` added to `Agent` struct (exported to frontend)
- `EscalationEvent` type carries `reason`, `turnCount`/`costUsd`, and `limit`
- `Guardrails` struct on `Manager`; set via `SetGuardrails()` wired from config in `app.go`
- **Turn guardrail**: count `assistant` events in `streamHeadlessOutput`; when `TurnCount >= MaxTurns`, emit `agent:escalation:{id}` then block on `escalationCh` waiting for human response
- **Cost guardrail**: at `result` event, if cumulative cost exceeds limit emit escalation (non-blocking — run already completed)
- `RespondEscalation(agentID, continueRun)` on `Manager` and `AgentService` sends human decision to unblock the channel

**Frontend**:
- `agentEscalation(id)` event helper in `events.ts`
- `AgentDetail.svelte` subscribes to escalation events; shows red banner with reason + limit
- Turn escalation: **Continue** (unblocks agent) and **Kill** buttons
- Cost escalation: **Dismiss** only (agent already stopped)

> Changelog: feat(agent): cost/turn guardrails with escalation

See discussion https://github.com/openhab/openhab-core/issues/5007

This is the first step to have all sitemap definitions in the UI and use core converters to convert to/from file formats.

This PR simply introduces a list of sitemaps as a separate tab on the pages list with specific functionality.:
- it will also show the unmanaged sitemaps in the list (non-editable).
- It introduces a copy to file definition button on the sitemaps tab, using the new REST endpoint from https://github.com/openhab/openhab-core/pull/5459
I opted to put the sitemaps in a separate list (next to Alphabetic and By Type). The reason is they are something totally different and cannot be used in the mainUI, I required specific logic (copy button only for sitemaps) and I didn't want to create another entry in settings to separate them out as it is to define UIs after all. Also, keeping it on the same level took less space in the UI then introducing another tab one level up to distinguish between mainUI widgets and sitemaps. Of course, this can be debated.

Next steps will be in a separate PR, building on top of this:
- ability to show unmanged sitemaps in the sitemap editor (all fields read only).
- replacing all DSL parsing and generation in the UI code by calls to the sitemap REST API.
- refactoring and improvements in the sitemap editor UI, such as better editors for rules and mappings, separating the format string from the label and editor with validation for the format string, etc.
A large part of that code is done, but as this will be a larger refactoring, I want to keep this separate.
